records.title: Message Flows
records.source_span_text:
6.3.3       Message Flows
During each ISA lifecycle phase, there are one or more series of message exchanges
(message flows) that will or could occur between the ISA component that initiated a
connection and the connected-to ISA Controller. This section presents a set of message
flows that is intended to address all common interactions between ISA components and ISA
Controllers, including for both sunny-day and rainy-day scenarios. Each message flow is
confined to a particular communication purpose.

The message flow diagrams provide only the key content of a message for a particular
interaction. The full message content is specified in the ISA DMS for ISA messages and the
ISA ICD for IPL messages.

The message flows are presented as Department of Defense (DoD) Architectural
Framework (DoDAF) Service View (SvcV) viewpoints, specifically Services Event-Trace
Description (SvcV-10c) viewpoints. The diagrams represent ISA components and ISA
services as lanes. Lanes for core ISA services are highlighted in aqua blue to indicate their
implementation by an ISA Controller. The lanes contain functions that are involved in the



                                                                                                28
 message exchange. The functions are purely illustrative, intended only to achieve an
understanding of the message exchanges that occur for a particular purpose. The functions,
and information shown being passed between functions within a lane, do not dictate
implementation thereof.

The message flow diagrams are intended to be read from left to right. The start of a
message flow is depicted by a circle with pink fill or a pink fringe. The end of a message
flow is depicted by a circle with a thick black boundary or a pointer to another message
flow. If a message flow results in a transition between ISA lifecycle phases for an ISA
component, the phases are indicated in the diagram. Conditions that dictate behavior are
presented in turquoise boxes.


6.3.3.1       Connection

6.3.3.1.1     Connection and Format Establishment
An ISA component initiates establishment of a secure, reliable connection to a selected ISA
Controller and negotiates the presentation format to be used for the connection with the
Controller.


Figure 7 - Connection and Format Establishment




                                                                                             29
 6.3.3.2      Registration

6.3.3.2.1    Registration
Upon establishment of a connection and presentation format, an ISA component requests
registration with the connected-to ISA Controller in order to join the ISA network of which
the Controller is a part.


Figure 8 - Registration




                                                                                          30
 6.3.3.2.2    Connection Termination on Missing Registration
If an ISA component does not send a Registration message within a certain time since a
presentation format is established for a connection, the ISA Controller terminates the
connection.


Figure 9 - Connection Termination on Missing Registration




6.3.3.2.3    Registration Renewal
An ISA Controller could request that a registered ISA component renew its registration,
which could happen, for instance, if the Controller believes that it is, or might be, out of
sync with the component. Note that such a request could arrive while the ISA component is
in the Registration, Configuration, or Operational phase.




                                                                                               31
 Figure 10 - Registration Renewal




6.3.3.3      Configuration

6.3.3.3.1    Initial Configuration
An ISA component and ISA Controller exchange CCDs containing declarations of all of the
ISA-visible observables, commands, and properties that they support, as well as the
readiness and reporting states of each of these declared capabilities.




                                                                                          32
 Figure 11 - Initial Configuration




6.3.3.3.2     Forced Deregistration on Missing Initial Configuration
If an ISA component does not send an initial Config message within a certain time since it
was registered, the ISA Controller deregisters the component.




                                                                                             33
 Figure 12 - Forced Deregistration on Missing Initial Configuration




6.3.3.3.3    Configuration Change by ISA Component
If the set of declarations of an ISA component (that is not an ISA Controller) changes in any
way and/or any readiness, and/or reporting states change for a capability that it declared,
the component submits an updated configuration to the connected-to ISA Controller.




                                                                                            34
 Figure 13 - Configuration Change by ISA Component




6.3.3.3.4   Configuration Change by ISA Controller
If an ISA Controller’s set of declarations changes in any way and/or any readiness, and/or
reporting states change for a capability that it declared, the Controller submits an updated
configuration to all connected-to ISA components.




                                                                                             35
 Figure 14 - Configuration Change by ISA Controller




6.3.3.3.5    Service Recommendation
An ISA component can implicitly request that a connected-to ISA Controller recommend an
instance of a Live Data Service and/or Authorization Service to use. A component
accomplishes this by declaring support of the Set Live Data Service and Set Authorization
Service commands in a Config message.




                                                                                            36
 Figure 15 - Service Recommendation




6.3.3.4     Status Reporting

6.3.3.4.1   Initial Status Reporting
Upon exchanging declarations, an ISA component and ISA Controller exchange the values of
all of their declared properties.




                                                                                      37
 Figure 16 - Initial Status Reporting




6.3.3.4.2     Forced Deregistration on Missing Initial Status
If an ISA component does not send an initial Status message within a certain time since it
was registered, the ISA Controller deregisters the component.




                                                                                             38
 Figure 17 - Forced Deregistration on Missing Initial Status




6.3.3.4.3    Periodic Status by ISA Component
After reporting its initial status, an ISA component periodically reports to the connected-to
ISA Controller any changes to the values of their declared properties that occurred since
the last status report. A status report must be sent even if no changes occurred, since the
report is also used by the ISA Controller to monitor the availability of the connected
component.




                                                                                              39
 Figure 18 - Periodic Status by ISA Component




6.3.3.4.4    Periodic Status by ISA Controller
After reporting its initial status, an ISA Controller periodically reports to the connected ISA
component any changes to the values of their declared properties that occurred since the
last status report. A status report must be sent even if no changes occurred.




                                                                                              40
 Figure 19 - Periodic Status by ISA Controller




6.3.3.4.5    Registration Revival on Missing Periodic Status
If an ISA component does not submit a status report within a specified timeout period since
the last status report was submitted (in which case the component is considered to be non-
responsive), the ISA Controller announces this condition, which the ISA component must
react to by submitting a status report. If the ISA component submits a status report within
a timeout period of receiving the announcement, the component is considered to be
revived and allowed to remain in the ISA network. Paragraph 6.3.3.4.6, Forced
Deregistration on Missing Periodic Status, describes when happens when the ISA
component fails to submit a status report in time.




                                                                                              41
 Figure 20 - Registration Revival on Missing Periodic Status




6.3.3.4.6    Forced Deregistration on Missing Periodic Status
If an ISA component does not submit a status report within a specified timeout period since
receiving a registration renewal request from the ISA Controller, the Controller forcibly
deregisters the component.




                                                                                            42
 Figure 21 - Forced Deregistration on Missing Periodic Status




6.3.3.5      Component Discovery
An ISA component could request information regarding ISA components of interest that are
available. As part of this request, a component can obtain the Config and Status messages
for the discovered components.




                                                                                            43
 Figure 22 - Component Discovery




                                  44
 6.3.3.6      Subscriptions

6.3.3.6.1    Subscription Creation

Figure 23 - Subscription Creation




6.3.3.6.2    Subscription Removal
An ISA component with a subscription could remove the subscription at any point but must
remove the subscription prior to requesting deregistration.




                                                                                      45
 Figure 24 - Subscription Removal




6.3.3.6.3   Subscribed-to Message Delivery
When an ISA component has created a subscription, the component will receive ISA
messages that match the subscription criteria. The Administrative, Config, Status, and
Event messages are the ISA messages that can be received for a subscription.




                                                                                         46
 Figure 25 - Subscribed-to Message Delivery




6.3.3.7      Observation Publication

6.3.3.7.1    Observation Publication
An ISA component publishes observables to the connected-to ISA Controller when it makes
observations. The ISA component previously declared the observables via a Config
message.




                                                                                      47
 Figure 26 - Observation Publication




6.3.3.7.2    Observation Update
An ISA component could update an Event message that it previously published. The Event
message that serves as the update cites the Event message being updated via the Shared
Event Reference (SER), contains zero or more updated versions of the observable(s) from
the cited Event message, and contains zero or more new observables. For each updated




                                                                                          48
 observable, an ISA component receiving such an Event message should stop using the
previous observable information and start using the new information.

Figure 27 applies for all sources of the observation update.


Figure 27 - Observation Update




6.3.3.7.3   Observation Recall
An ISA component could recall an Event message that it previously published. The Event
message that serves as the recall cites the Event message being recalled via the SER and




                                                                                           49
 contains the Recall observable. An ISA component receiving such an Event message should
cease using all observable information from the recalled Event message.

Figure 28 applies for all sources of the observation recall.


Figure 28 - Observation Recall




                                                                                      50
 6.3.3.8     Command Execution
An ISA component could receive commands for a variety of purposes, including commands
destined for itself and commands destined for virtual ISA components for which it is a CIC.
An ISA Controller’s handling of commands destined for services that the Controller
provides are addressed in the corresponding section herein.

6.3.3.8.1   Command Execution by ISA Component
An ISA component must be able to handle commands destined for it. There are a number of
potential outcomes of requests to execute commands, depending on the validity of a
Request message, the current state of the performing component (e.g., whether it is busy),
the functionality of the performing component (e.g., whether it supports command
queuing), and whether the command was successfully executed. Also, for commands that
cannot be executed immediately (and therefore are queued, if supported), that take a while
to execute, or that are inherently long-standing, the performing component would provide
intermediate responses that indicate the status of the execution of the command (queued
or in progress) and any intermediate results.

Timers govern how soon after a Request message is received that a (initial) Response
message must be sent and how often intermediate Response messages must be sent. Also, if
a Request message contains a stale time within which a command must be completed, the
performing ISA component sets a timer accordingly.




                                                                                             51
 Figure 29 - Command Execution by ISA Component




                                                 52
 6.3.3.8.2   Command Authorization
When authorization of a command is necessary, the Communication Service requests the
Authorization Service to determine if the requesting component is authorized to request
the execution of the command by the performing component. There are a small number of
commands for which authorization is not necessary.


Figure 30 - Command Authorization




6.3.3.9     Graceful Deregistration
An ISA component must request deregistration when it intends to leave the ISA network to
which it is joined (e.g., prior to shutdown).




                                                                                          53
 Figure 31 - Graceful Deregistration




6.3.3.10     Virtual ISA Component Management
As described in paragraph 4.2.2, ISA Compositions, an ISA component could play the role of
a CIC for virtual ISA components.

6.3.3.10.1 Virtual ISA Component Joining
If a virtual ISA component has become available to the CIC, the CIC announces the
availability of the component and submits a configuration and status report for it.




                                                                                        54
 Figure 32 - Virtual ISA Component Joining




                                            55
 6.3.3.10.2 Virtual ISA Component Leaving
If a virtual ISA component becomes unavailable to the CIC, the CIC announces the loss of
availability of the component.


Figure 33 - Virtual ISA Component Leaving




                                                                                           56
 6.3.3.10.3 Observation Publication for Virtual ISA Component
If an ISA component plays the role of a CIC for a virtual ISA component, and the virtual ISA
component produces observables, the CIC publishes observables to the ISA Controller on
behalf of the virtual ISA component.


Figure 34 - Observation Publication for Virtual ISA Component




                                                                                           57
records.source_locator: ISA Software Design Document 6.0r5 (31 October 2023), §6.3.3 Message Flows, PDF36–65 / printed28–57
records.source_span_hash_basis: Exact UTF-8 span provided in sdd_exact_spans.json, boundaries 67974–83563 in registered source extraction. Contains all nested message-flow text and captions; diagram pixels separately inspected and hashed.
records.meaning: Purpose-specific illustrative message exchanges describe connection, registration, configuration, status/liveness, discovery, subscriptions, observation publication/revision/recall, command execution/authorization, graceful leaving and CIC-mediated virtual-component participation.
native_rules: Diagrams supply only key message content; full ISA messages are specified by DMS and IPL messages by ICD.
DoDAF SvcV-10c lanes represent components/services; aqua core-service lanes indicate Controller implementation. Internal functions and intra-lane information do not dictate implementation.

Read left to right. Pink-filled/fringed circle starts; thick black boundary circle or another-flow pointer ends; turquoise conditions govern branches. Lifecycle phases are labelled when a flow effects a transition.
Authentication, authorization, registration, capability declarations, readiness/reporting states, property values and command outcomes are distinct.
Initial and changed/periodic Status reporting differ; no-change periodic Status still must be sent. Receipt is network communication evidence, not physical health proof.
Registration renewal, communication revival, forced deregistration and graceful deregistration are different flows and have different connection/cache consequences.

Publication/update/recall are Event-message scenarios; recipients should replace updated observable information or cease recalled-event use. Source does not demonstrate recipient compliance or delete histories.
Command execution allows conditional queueing and intermediate responses with separate initial, periodic and stale-command timers; authorization decision success may still mean permission denied.
Virtual-member availability and observations can be represented by a CIC while payload identity remains that of the subcomponent/producer.
limitations: No implementation conformance test, actual network registration, device action, permission grant, observation or measured physical effect occurred in this review.
Do not convert logical network/service roles into physical chassis containment or mandatory adoption of the ISA architecture as DIM.
Detailed DMS command/type evidence remains authoritative for saved native structures; SDD schematic naming differences retained as local wording notes.
Source examples do not enumerate every legal field, response, option, transport or authorization exception; missing optional diagram detail is not automatically a contradiction.

This review covers only registered SDD-6.3.3. Shared PDF36 Figure6 belongs prior lifecycle block and is not claimed as a second registered review. External standards and later source blocks not reopened.
No new primary question or adoption decision introduced; existing six primary questions, case uncertainties, donor boundaries and current workbook snapshot untouched.

nested_flows.title: Connection and Format Establishment
nested_flows.source_span_text:
6.3.3.1.1     Connection and Format Establishment
An ISA component initiates establishment of a secure, reliable connection to a selected ISA
Controller and negotiates the presentation format to be used for the connection with the
Controller.


Figure 7 - Connection and Format Establishment




                                                                                             29
nested_flows.trigger_or_entry: Disconnected component initiates connection to selected Controller; identification may be local configuration or Controller detection by querying/listening.

ordered_exchange_and_branches.description: Joiner Initiate Connection and Communication Service Negotiate Connection exchange connection request, connection setup and security setup. Actual messages depend on transport/security protocols.
Connection setup or security setup failure branches to Error. Security setup success proceeds to presentation-format negotiation.
Joiner sends IPL Handshake Begin; service Negotiate Format returns IPL Error on negotiation failure or IPL Handshake Complete on success.
Successful format negotiation leaves joiner Connected; Communication Service starts Registration Receipt Timer after sending IPL Handshake Complete.

conditions_timers_and_modal_rules: Registration receipt timer is configurable; no numeric interval stated.
Transport/security-message detail is referred to ICD, not specified by this figure.
source_described_state_and_registry_effe: Disconnected → Connected only on shown successful establishment/negotiation path; error alternatives shown.
limits_and_distinctions: Connected is not Registered, Configured or Operational.
No security-protocol implementation or actual connection is verified.

nested_flows.title: Registration
nested_flows.source_span_text:
6.3.3.2.1    Registration
Upon establishment of a connection and presentation format, an ISA component requests
registration with the connected-to ISA Controller in order to join the ISA network of which
the Controller is a part.


Figure 8 - Registration




                                                                                          30
nested_flows.trigger_or_entry: Connected component requests permission to join the Controller network.

ordered_exchange_and_branches.description: Registrant sends Registration with source = Registrant UCI and opcode = REQUEST ADD to Communication Service Register Component.
Communication Service authenticates registrant. Failure returns Registration opcode = ERROR.
If authenticated, Communication Service checks authorization of joining with Authorization Service: diagram Request is labelled command = Authorize, header & message = received Registration message.

Authorization Service returns Response: authorized=yes/type=SUCCESS when permitted; authorized=no/type=SUCCESS when denied; type=FAILED when unable to perform authorization. Denied or unable paths yield Registration ERROR.
Authorized join yields Registration ADDED, starts Configuration Receipt Timer, and announces Administrative about=Registrant UCI/code=DEVICE ADDED to Live Data Service.
Live Data Service creates registry record for the UCI and sends the administrative notification into Subscribed-to Message Delivery.

conditions_timers_and_modal_rules: Config receipt timer is configurable and begins after Registration ADDED is sent.
Authentication, permission decision, registration result and subsequent Config receipt are separate stages.
source_described_state_and_registry_effe: Shown successful endpoint Registered; Live Data registry creation is logical component record creation.
limits_and_distinctions: Authorizing operation SUCCESS with authorized=no is a successfully obtained denial, not permission to join.
No universal credential schema or hardware attachment is supplied by the figure.

nested_flows.title: Connection Termination on Missing Registration
nested_flows.source_span_text:
6.3.3.2.2    Connection Termination on Missing Registration
If an ISA component does not send a Registration message within a certain time since a
presentation format is established for a connection, the ISA Controller terminates the
connection.


Figure 9 - Connection Termination on Missing Registration
nested_flows.trigger_or_entry: Registration Receipt Timer expires without Registration after established format.

ordered_exchange_and_branches.description: Communication Service passes expired Registration Receipt Timer to Register Component, then Terminate Connection.
Note states joiner is Disconnected upon termination.

conditions_timers_and_modal_rules: Missing Registration is measured from presentation-format establishment; timer value configurable in Figure 7.
source_described_state_and_registry_effe: Connection terminated; joiner Disconnected.
limits_and_distinctions: No prior successful registration or network-record removal is implied.
No device power loss or physical removal is inferred.

figure_observation.caption: Figure 9 - Connection Termination on Missing Registration

nested_flows.title: Registration Renewal
nested_flows.source_span_text:
6.3.3.2.3    Registration Renewal
An ISA Controller could request that a registered ISA component renew its registration,
which could happen, for instance, if the Controller believes that it is, or might be, out of
sync with the component. Note that such a request could arrive while the ISA component is
in the Registration, Configuration, or Operational phase.




                                                                                               31
 Figure 10 - Registration Renewal
nested_flows.trigger_or_entry: Controller may believe it is, or could be, out of synchronization with a registered component.

ordered_exchange_and_branches.description: Communication Service Request Registration Renewal sends Registration opcode=RENEW.
Registrant Register with ISA Network redirects to the Registration flow, Figure 8.

conditions_timers_and_modal_rules: Prose allows request during Registration, Configuration or Operational phases; figure note uses Registered, Configured or Operational states.
source_described_state_and_registry_effe: Renewal requests re-registration; it is not the NON RESPONSIVE/Status/REVIVED exchange.
limits_and_distinctions: No automatic successful renewal, timer duration, status revival or preserved permission is assumed.

figure_observation.caption: Figure 10 - Registration Renewal

nested_flows.title: Initial Configuration
nested_flows.source_span_text:
6.3.3.3.1    Initial Configuration
An ISA component and ISA Controller exchange CCDs containing declarations of all of the
ISA-visible observables, commands, and properties that they support, as well as the
readiness and reporting states of each of these declared capabilities.




                                                                                          32
 Figure 11 - Initial Configuration
nested_flows.trigger_or_entry: Registered component and Controller exchange CCD declarations and capability readiness/reporting states.

ordered_exchange_and_branches.description: Registrant Declare Capabilities sends Config containing declarations and states for all exposed registrant capabilities. Figure shows Registered → Configured following Declare Capabilities.
Communication Service receives valid Config before Configuration Receipt Timer expiry, returns its Config for all exposed Controller capabilities, and starts Initial Status Receipt Timer.
Registrant receives Controller declarations. Communication Service forwards registrant Config to Live Data Service.
Live Data Service adds Config contents to registry record for UCI and invokes Subscribed-to Message Delivery.

conditions_timers_and_modal_rules: Initial Status receipt timer configurable; explicitly starts after receiving registrant Config.
Prose: all ISA-visible observables, commands and properties supported, plus declared capability readiness/reporting states.
source_described_state_and_registry_effe: Capability/configuration cache populated; no property-value Status yet in this flow.
limits_and_distinctions: Declared support is not actual command execution or readiness of all catalogue commands.
Config is distinct from instructions that physically configure equipment.

nested_flows.title: Forced Deregistration on Missing Initial Configuration
nested_flows.source_span_text:
6.3.3.3.2     Forced Deregistration on Missing Initial Configuration
If an ISA component does not send an initial Config message within a certain time since it
was registered, the ISA Controller deregisters the component.




                                                                                             33
 Figure 12 - Forced Deregistration on Missing Initial Configuration
nested_flows.trigger_or_entry: Configuration Receipt Timer expires without initial Config after registration.

ordered_exchange_and_branches.description: Communication Service Receive Declarations sees no Config, invokes Deregister Component, and sends Registration opcode=REMOVED to registrant.
Registrant is shown Deregistered; Communication Service terminates connection, with note that registrant becomes Disconnected.
Communication Service announces Administrative about=Registrant UCI/code=DEVICE REMOVED to Live Data Service.
Live Data Service deletes registry record for UCI and invokes subscribed-to delivery for the Administrative notification.

conditions_timers_and_modal_rules: Removal notification arrives while registrant is Registered.
source_described_state_and_registry_effe: Logical registration removed, connection terminated, registry record deleted.
limits_and_distinctions: Does not prove hardware disappeared or delete historic observations.
Figure does not itself show subscription-table cleanup for this initial-Config failure.

figure_observation.caption: Figure 12 - Forced Deregistration on Missing Initial Configuration

nested_flows.title: Configuration Change by ISA Component
nested_flows.source_span_text:
6.3.3.3.3    Configuration Change by ISA Component
If the set of declarations of an ISA component (that is not an ISA Controller) changes in any
way and/or any readiness, and/or reporting states change for a capability that it declared,
the component submits an updated configuration to the connected-to ISA Controller.




                                                                                            34
 Figure 13 - Configuration Change by ISA Component
nested_flows.trigger_or_entry: A non-Controller component changes any declarations or readiness/reporting states while Configured or Operational.

ordered_exchange_and_branches.description: Registrant Declare Capabilities emits Config when declarations and/or states change to any extent. If declarations change, whole CCD is included; if ready/reporting states change, the changes are included.
Registrant then Report Status emits changes since last sent Status, including changes resulting from configuration changes.
Communication Service receives declarations and Status and forwards Config/Status to Live Data Service.
Live Data Service updates UCI registry record with Config and Status contents and invokes subscribed-to delivery for both.

conditions_timers_and_modal_rules: Declaration replacement scope and state-change scope differ.
Change-triggered report is not a mandate to republish all property values.
source_described_state_and_registry_effe: Registry represents new configuration and latest accumulated reported status.
limits_and_distinctions: No physical parameter-setting command is performed by merely reporting Config.
No deleted or unavailable data is invented from omitted fields.

figure_observation.caption: Figure 13 - Configuration Change by ISA Component

nested_flows.title: Configuration Change by ISA Controller
nested_flows.source_span_text:
6.3.3.3.4   Configuration Change by ISA Controller
If an ISA Controller’s set of declarations changes in any way and/or any readiness, and/or
reporting states change for a capability that it declared, the Controller submits an updated
configuration to all connected-to ISA components.




                                                                                             35
 Figure 14 - Configuration Change by ISA Controller
nested_flows.trigger_or_entry: Controller changes any declarations or readiness/reporting states.

ordered_exchange_and_branches.description: Controller Declare Capabilities sends updated Config to all connected-to ISA components per prose: whole CCD if declarations changed, changes for ready/reporting states.
Controller Report Status sends changes since last sent Status, including configuration changes.
Registrant receives declarations then Status; note allows receipt while Configured or Operational.

conditions_timers_and_modal_rules: Trigger is declarations/states changed to any extent.
source_described_state_and_registry_effe: Clients receive Controller capability/state update.
limits_and_distinctions: No all-services-mandatory claim; no physical enclosure change.
Figure is a directed example lane; all connected-to recipients are supplied by prose.

figure_observation.caption: Figure 14 - Configuration Change by ISA Controller

nested_flows.title: Service Recommendation
nested_flows.source_span_text:
6.3.3.3.5    Service Recommendation
An ISA component can implicitly request that a connected-to ISA Controller recommend an
instance of a Live Data Service and/or Authorization Service to use. A component
accomplishes this by declaring support of the Set Live Data Service and Set Authorization
Service commands in a Config message.




                                                                                            36
 Figure 15 - Service Recommendation
nested_flows.trigger_or_entry: Registrant CCD declares Set Authorization Service and/or Set Live Data Service, and Controller has a provider instance to recommend.

ordered_exchange_and_branches.description: After sending its initial Status to registrant, Controller Recommend Service sends one Request per recommended service.
Request command=Set Authorization Service or Set Live Data Service, service=UCI of recommended service instance.
Registrant Receive Service Recommendation responds type=SUCCESS if successful or FAILED if unsuccessful.

conditions_timers_and_modal_rules: Component is NOT required to request recommendations for services it can use, NOR required to use a recommended service.
Shown path requires declared recommendation-command support and available provider.
source_described_state_and_registry_effe: Recommendation delivered/processed; choice of actual provider remains separate.
limits_and_distinctions: SUCCESS does not establish actual provider use, authorization or registration.
DMS optional service omission means no acceptable provider; shown positive-provider flow is not exhaustive.

nested_flows.title: Initial Status Reporting
nested_flows.source_span_text:
6.3.3.4.1   Initial Status Reporting
Upon exchanging declarations, an ISA component and ISA Controller exchange the values of
all of their declared properties.




                                                                                      37
 Figure 16 - Initial Status Reporting
nested_flows.trigger_or_entry: Configured component has exchanged declarations and reports initial property values.

ordered_exchange_and_branches.description: Registrant sends Status containing values for all declared properties that are ready and being reported, and sets its Status Reporting Timer between Minimum and Maximum Status Interval.

Communication Service accepts valid Status before Initial Status Receipt Timer expiry, starts Periodic Status Receipt Timer, and returns Controller Status containing all declared ready/reporting property values.
Controller starts its own Status Reporting Timer between Minimum and Maximum Status Interval values it reported to the component. Registrant receives Status and reaches Operational in the diagram.
Registrant Status is passed to Live Data Service, added to its UCI registry record and passed to subscribed-to delivery.

conditions_timers_and_modal_rules: Periodic Status Receipt Timer is configurable multiplier of Maximum Status Interval last reported by registrant.
Figure qualifies property selection as declared AND ready AND reporting; prose on preceding page says all declared properties.
source_described_state_and_registry_effe: Configured → Operational on shown initial exchange; registry gains reported status.
limits_and_distinctions: Operational is protocol lifecycle, not proof all equipment functions are ready.
Periodic/initial publication differs from Get Status command, which retrieves declared-ready properties even if reporting disabled.
No numeric timer/default inferred.

nested_flows.title: Forced Deregistration on Missing Initial Status
nested_flows.source_span_text:
6.3.3.4.2     Forced Deregistration on Missing Initial Status
If an ISA component does not send an initial Status message within a certain time since it
was registered, the ISA Controller deregisters the component.




                                                                                             38
 Figure 17 - Forced Deregistration on Missing Initial Status
nested_flows.trigger_or_entry: Initial Status Receipt Timer expires without initial Status.

ordered_exchange_and_branches.description: Communication Service Receive Status sees no Status, invokes Deregister Component and sends Registration opcode=REMOVED.
Registrant receives removal while Configured and becomes Deregistered; service terminates connection, with note that registrant becomes Disconnected.
Administrative about=Registrant UCI/code=DEVICE REMOVED goes to Live Data Service.
Live Data Service deletes registry record for UCI and invokes subscribed-to delivery.

conditions_timers_and_modal_rules: §6.3.3.4.2 prose says timeout since registered; Figure 11 starts this timer after Config receipt. Both statements retained.
source_described_state_and_registry_effe: Deregistration and connection termination; logical registry record removed.
limits_and_distinctions: No hardware-failure diagnosis or deletion of historical measurements.
No assumption that absent timely receipt proves no Status was generated.

figure_observation.caption: Figure 17 - Forced Deregistration on Missing Initial Status

nested_flows.title: Periodic Status by ISA Component
nested_flows.source_span_text:
6.3.3.4.3    Periodic Status by ISA Component
After reporting its initial status, an ISA component periodically reports to the connected-to
ISA Controller any changes to the values of their declared properties that occurred since
the last status report. A status report must be sent even if no changes occurred, since the
report is also used by the ISA Controller to monitor the availability of the connected
component.




                                                                                              39
 Figure 18 - Periodic Status by ISA Component
nested_flows.trigger_or_entry: Registrant Periodic Status Reporting Timer expires after initial reporting.

ordered_exchange_and_branches.description: Registrant Report Status sends ONLY changed values since last status report for declared properties that are ready and being reported.
Communication Service Receive Status restarts Periodic Status Receipt Timer and passes Status to Live Data Service.
Live Data Service updates UCI registry record using Status contents and invokes subscribed-to delivery.

conditions_timers_and_modal_rules: Status must be sent even when no values changed; receipt also monitors communication availability.
source_described_state_and_registry_effe: Receipt deadline restarted; accumulated current status cache updated.
limits_and_distinctions: No-change Status is not a new observation or proof of physical health.
Changed-value reporting is not a complete snapshot on every transmission.

figure_observation.caption: Figure 18 - Periodic Status by ISA Component
figure_observation.diagram_internal_title: Periodic Status Reporting by ISA Component

nested_flows.title: Periodic Status by ISA Controller
nested_flows.source_span_text:
6.3.3.4.4    Periodic Status by ISA Controller
After reporting its initial status, an ISA Controller periodically reports to the connected ISA
component any changes to the values of their declared properties that occurred since the
last status report. A status report must be sent even if no changes occurred.




                                                                                              40
 Figure 19 - Periodic Status by ISA Controller
nested_flows.trigger_or_entry: Controller Periodic Status Reporting Timer expires after initial reporting.

ordered_exchange_and_branches.description: Controller sends Status containing ONLY changed values since last report for declared properties that are ready and being reported.
Registrant receives Controller Status while Operational.

conditions_timers_and_modal_rules: Controller must send Status even if no changes occurred.
source_described_state_and_registry_effe: Continued Controller property reporting.
limits_and_distinctions: Figure does not show symmetrical client-side revival/deregistration enforcement; do not invent it.
No complete snapshot or observation sampling interval implied.

figure_observation.caption: Figure 19 - Periodic Status by ISA Controller
figure_observation.diagram_internal_title: Periodic Status Reporting by ISA Controller

nested_flows.title: Registration Revival on Missing Periodic Status
nested_flows.source_span_text:
6.3.3.4.5    Registration Revival on Missing Periodic Status
If an ISA component does not submit a status report within a specified timeout period since
the last status report was submitted (in which case the component is considered to be non-
responsive), the ISA Controller announces this condition, which the ISA component must
react to by submitting a status report. If the ISA component submits a status report within
a timeout period of receiving the announcement, the component is considered to be
revived and allowed to remain in the ISA network. Paragraph 6.3.3.4.6, Forced
Deregistration on Missing Periodic Status, describes when happens when the ISA
component fails to submit a status report in time.




                                                                                              41
 Figure 20 - Registration Revival on Missing Periodic Status
nested_flows.trigger_or_entry: Periodic Status Receipt Timer expires with no Status from Operational registrant.

ordered_exchange_and_branches.description: Communication Service Receive Status invokes Revive Component; sends Registration opcode=NON RESPONSIVE and announces Administrative about=Registrant UCI/code=DEVICE NON RESPONSIVE.
Communication Service starts Revival Status Receipt Timer; registrant Register with ISA Network responds to non-responsive indication by Report Status.

If Status arrives within revival timeout, Communication Service sends Registration opcode=REVIVED, announces Administrative code=DEVICE REVIVED, stops revival timer and restarts periodic receipt timer.
Registrant, upon revival, sends Config with declarations and states for all registrant capabilities.
Status, revived Config and Administrative notifications reach Live Data Service; registry receives Status and Config updates and the messages enter subscribed-to delivery.

conditions_timers_and_modal_rules: Periodic and revival receipt timers use configurable multipliers of last reported Maximum Status Interval.
Prose: component must react to non-responsive announcement by submitting Status; timely receipt allows it to remain in network.
source_described_state_and_registry_effe: Logical communication revival and continued registration; refreshed configuration/status cache.
limits_and_distinctions: NON RESPONSIVE does not prove physical failure; REVIVED does not prove sensor accuracy or repaired equipment.
Renewal (RENEW → Registration) and revival (NON RESPONSIVE → Status → REVIVED) are distinct.
No timer multiplier or exact scheduling implementation supplied.

figure_observation.caption: Figure 20 - Registration Revival on Missing Periodic Status

nested_flows.title: Forced Deregistration on Missing Periodic Status
nested_flows.source_span_text:
6.3.3.4.6    Forced Deregistration on Missing Periodic Status
If an ISA component does not submit a status report within a specified timeout period since
receiving a registration renewal request from the ISA Controller, the Controller forcibly
deregisters the component.




                                                                                            42
 Figure 21 - Forced Deregistration on Missing Periodic Status
nested_flows.trigger_or_entry: Periodic Status receipt timeout followed by lack of timely Status during revival window.

ordered_exchange_and_branches.description: Periodic Status Receipt Timer expiry with no Status invokes Revive Component, Registration NON RESPONSIVE and Administrative DEVICE NON RESPONSIVE, and starts Revival Status Receipt Timer.
If revival receipt timer expires with no Status, Communication Service deregisters component, sends Registration REMOVED, announces Administrative DEVICE REMOVED, and terminates connection.
Registrant is shown Deregistered and, after connection termination, Disconnected.
Live Data Service delivers notifications to matching subscriptions, deletes registry record for UCI and removes any subscriptions for that UCI from Subscription Table.

conditions_timers_and_modal_rules: Revival receipt timeout is configurable multiplier of last reported Maximum Status Interval.
Prose names a registration renewal request; actual figure shows NON RESPONSIVE and revival timer, not RENEW.
source_described_state_and_registry_effe: Logical deregistration, connection termination, registry/subscription cleanup.
limits_and_distinctions: No physical removal, hardware reset or archive/history deletion inferred.
No subscriber privacy/access policy or unknown-ID cleanup rule inferred.

figure_observation.caption: Figure 21 - Forced Deregistration on Missing Periodic Status

nested_flows.title: Component Discovery
nested_flows.source_span_text:
6.3.3.5      Component Discovery
An ISA component could request information regarding ISA components of interest that are
available. As part of this request, a component can obtain the Config and Status messages
for the discovered components.




                                                                                            43
 Figure 22 - Component Discovery




                                  44
nested_flows.trigger_or_entry: Requester seeks currently available components and optionally Config/Status.

ordered_exchange_and_branches.description: Requester Discover Available Assets sends Request command=Discover, script=filtering script for desired data.
Communication Service Broker Request invokes Command Authorization. If not authorized returns Response PERMISSION DENIED; if authorized forwards Discover request to Live Data Service.
Live Data Service queries Registry using filtering script; diagram shows UCIs and requested Config/Status for matching components.

Service returns Response SUCCESS with ucis of matching components; unsuccessful response codes referred to DMS. If requested via script and matches exist, Config and Status are separately drawn with to=Requester UCI.
Communication Service forwards responses and Config/Status to requester; success or failure endpoints are shown.

conditions_timers_and_modal_rules: Config/Status retrieval conditional on request and matches.
source_described_state_and_registry_effe: Read/query of available registry information; no new subscription or historical result cache created by this figure.
limits_and_distinctions: Literal script/ucis diagram names are not silently substituted for DMS query/include ucis/components/messages contract.
Diagram does not override full DMS return representation or guarantee component physical availability.

nested_flows.title: Subscription Creation
nested_flows.source_span_text:
6.3.3.6.1    Subscription Creation

Figure 23 - Subscription Creation
nested_flows.trigger_or_entry: Subscriber requests future matching messages.

ordered_exchange_and_branches.description: Subscriber sends Request command=Add Subscription, query=filtering script for desired data.
Communication Service checks authorization: PERMISSION DENIED if not authorized, otherwise forwards request to Live Data Service.
Live Data Service Maintain Subscriptions adds entry to Subscription Table and returns SUCCESS with assigned subscription id; unsuccessful codes referred to DMS.
On successful creation, Maintain Configuration and Status queries Registry and emits any Config and Status messages matching query; Communication Service forwards these and response to subscriber.

conditions_timers_and_modal_rules: Figure depicts initial cached Config/Status delivery; DQL without cache can suppress initial cached-message values.
Full DMS optional name/consumer and replacement behavior remain valid although omitted from key-content diagram.
source_described_state_and_registry_effe: Subscription table entry created/updated under full saved command contract; initial cache delivery and future delivery remain distinct.
limits_and_distinctions: Subscription ID is creator/consumer/name structure, not assumed number or globally unique bare name.
Figure showing subscriber as consumer does not eliminate separate creator/consumer support.
No proof of actual successful delivery or runtime parser behavior.

nested_flows.title: Subscription Removal
nested_flows.source_span_text:
6.3.3.6.2    Subscription Removal
An ISA component with a subscription could remove the subscription at any point but must
remove the subscription prior to requesting deregistration.




                                                                                      45
 Figure 24 - Subscription Removal
nested_flows.trigger_or_entry: Component removes subscription at any point; prose requires removal before requesting deregistration.

ordered_exchange_and_branches.description: Subscriber sends Request command=Remove Subscription, subscription ID=ID of subscription being removed.
Communication Service checks authorization, returns PERMISSION DENIED if denied, otherwise forwards Remove Subscription request.
Live Data Service Maintain Subscriptions deletes subscription with supplied ID from Subscription Table and returns SUCCESS or DMS-defined unsuccessful response.
Communication Service forwards response; requester shown success/error.

conditions_timers_and_modal_rules: Source function box remains labelled Subscribe to Messages despite removal purpose.
Must remove subscription before graceful deregistration per prose.
source_described_state_and_registry_effe: Active subscription removed.
limits_and_distinctions: Removal does not recall or delete past delivered messages.
Unknown-ID or retry/idempotency behavior not specified.

nested_flows.title: Subscribed-to Message Delivery
nested_flows.source_span_text:
6.3.3.6.3   Subscribed-to Message Delivery
When an ISA component has created a subscription, the component will receive ISA
messages that match the subscription criteria. The Administrative, Config, Status, and
Event messages are the ISA messages that can be received for a subscription.




                                                                                         46
 Figure 25 - Subscribed-to Message Delivery
nested_flows.trigger_or_entry: Administrative, Config, Status or Event arrives for subscription matching.

ordered_exchange_and_branches.description: Live Data Service Match Subscriptions compares incoming message with Subscription Table and obtains matching UCIs.
If a match occurs for any of four message kinds, service generates a corresponding message for each matched UCI; to=matched UCI, body=matched message.
Communication Service Forward Message routes Administrative/Config/Status/Event to subscriber Receive Subscribed-to Message; note assumes subscriber Operational.

conditions_timers_and_modal_rules: Delivery is conditional on matching; four supported message kinds explicitly shown.
Saved Data Query separates matching from projection/returned fields and options.
source_described_state_and_registry_effe: Selected subscribers receive routed messages in this design scenario.
limits_and_distinctions: Not an indiscriminate network-wide broadcast, nor evidence all subscribers receive every original field.
Request/Response/Registration union membership does not make them subscription-selectable here.
No exactly-once, retransmission, ordering or realized delivery guarantee asserted.

nested_flows.title: Observation Publication
nested_flows.source_span_text:
6.3.3.7.1    Observation Publication
An ISA component publishes observables to the connected-to ISA Controller when it makes
observations. The ISA component previously declared the observables via a Config
message.




                                                                                      47
 Figure 26 - Observation Publication
nested_flows.trigger_or_entry: Component makes observations of observables previously declared in Config.

ordered_exchange_and_branches.description: Publisher Publish Observation sends Event containing one or more observables declared by publisher.
Communication Service Route Message passes Event to Live Data Service.
Live Data Service invokes Subscribed-to Message Delivery.

conditions_timers_and_modal_rules: This publication scenario says one or more declared observables; saved Event structure permits required 0+ list generally.
source_described_state_and_registry_effe: Event publication and conditional subscribed delivery.
limits_and_distinctions: No general Event=performed OMS Observation equivalence, sampling-process proof or original resultTime inferred.
No Event cache or historical archive is shown; DQL explicitly says Event messages not cached.

nested_flows.title: Observation Update
nested_flows.source_span_text:
6.3.3.7.2    Observation Update
An ISA component could update an Event message that it previously published. The Event
message that serves as the update cites the Event message being updated via the Shared
Event Reference (SER), contains zero or more updated versions of the observable(s) from
the cited Event message, and contains zero or more new observables. For each updated




                                                                                          48
 observable, an ISA component receiving such an Event message should stop using the
previous observable information and start using the new information.

Figure 27 applies for all sources of the observation update.


Figure 27 - Observation Update
nested_flows.trigger_or_entry: Publisher updates an Event it previously published; figure applies to all sources of update.

ordered_exchange_and_branches.description: Publisher sends new Event with ser=ID of Event message being updated. Prose calls reference Shared Event Reference (SER).
Event contains zero or more updated versions of prior observables and zero or more new observables; added observables must NOT include Recall per figure.
Communication Service routes Event to Live Data Service, which invokes subscribed-to delivery.
For each updated observable, receiving component should stop using old observable information and start using new information.

conditions_timers_and_modal_rules: Replacement guidance is per updated observable; not an unconditional whole-message overwrite.
source_described_state_and_registry_effe: Published revision/reference and recipient guidance, not demonstrated recipient mutation.
limits_and_distinctions: Retain literal SER terminology; DMS Event uses event reference with creator/Event ID/time, not a proved alias of generic message ID.
No deletion of prior evidence, physical measurement rerun, universal update acceptance or recipient compliance inferred.

figure_observation.caption: Figure 27 - Observation Update
literal_key_labels_as_seen: ser = ID of Event message being updated
must NOT include the Recall observable

nested_flows.title: Observation Recall
nested_flows.source_span_text:
6.3.3.7.3   Observation Recall
An ISA component could recall an Event message that it previously published. The Event
message that serves as the recall cites the Event message being recalled via the SER and




                                                                                           49
 contains the Recall observable. An ISA component receiving such an Event message should
cease using all observable information from the recalled Event message.

Figure 28 applies for all sources of the observation recall.


Figure 28 - Observation Recall




                                                                                      50
nested_flows.trigger_or_entry: Publisher recalls an Event it previously published; figure applies to all sources of recall.

ordered_exchange_and_branches.description: Publisher sends new Event with ser=ID of Event message being recalled and the Recall observable.
Communication Service routes Event to Live Data Service, which invokes subscribed-to delivery.
Receiving component should cease using all observable information from the recalled Event per prose.

conditions_timers_and_modal_rules: Recall presence distinguishes recall from ordinary update; saved Recall observable is String reason referencing prior Event.
source_described_state_and_registry_effe: Recall indication and recipient use guidance.
limits_and_distinctions: Not a delete command, archive erasure, revoked physical observation or proof all recipients ceased use.
Literal SER remains separate from fully specified DMS Event Reference; no bare-ID equivalence introduced.

figure_observation.caption: Figure 28 - Observation Recall
literal_key_labels_as_seen: ser = ID of Event message being recalled

nested_flows.title: Command Execution by ISA Component
nested_flows.source_span_text:
6.3.3.8.1   Command Execution by ISA Component
An ISA component must be able to handle commands destined for it. There are a number of
potential outcomes of requests to execute commands, depending on the validity of a
Request message, the current state of the performing component (e.g., whether it is busy),
the functionality of the performing component (e.g., whether it supports command
queuing), and whether the command was successfully executed. Also, for commands that
cannot be executed immediately (and therefore are queued, if supported), that take a while
to execute, or that are inherently long-standing, the performing component would provide
intermediate responses that indicate the status of the execution of the command (queued
or in progress) and any intermediate results.

Timers govern how soon after a Request message is received that a (initial) Response
message must be sent and how often intermediate Response messages must be sent. Also, if
a Request message contains a stale time within which a command must be completed, the
performing ISA component sets a timer accordingly.




                                                                                             51
 Figure 29 - Command Execution by ISA Component




                                                 52
nested_flows.trigger_or_entry: Request commands performer; group prose includes self-destined commands and commands for virtual components whose CIC receives them.

ordered_exchange_and_branches.description: Requester sends Request with command=requested command and to=Performer UCI. Communication Service Broker Request invokes Command Authorization where needed; denied yields PERMISSION DENIED, authorized forwards original request.

Performer Check Validity and Support checks request validity, declared command availability, busy/queue support and whether stale deadline can be met. Figure lists BUSY, COMMAND NOT AVAILABLE, INVALID ARGS or INVALID COMMAND for validation/availability failures; full DMS also has INSUFFICIENT TIME.

Initial Response Timer starts when Request arrives; set to performer Minimum Status Interval and stopped if initial response sent before expiry. Valid executable Request with stale time starts Stale Command Timer.

If available execute; if busy but queueing possible and deadline might be met, Queue Command. Initial response before/upon initial timer expiry may be SUCCESS, IN PROGRESS or QUEUED according to execution status (or FAILED), with applicable return values.

For queued/long-standing commands, Periodic Response Timer starts with initial Response, resets with each subsequent Response, stops at execution completion; interval is performer Maximum Status Interval.
While queued, periodic response is QUEUED. On queued command execution and while running, SUCCESS or IN PROGRESS (or FAILED) is returned as applicable; periodic running responses are IN PROGRESS.

Long-running command can emit IN PROGRESS with intermediate values when information is available. Stale Command Timer expiry before completion yields FAILED. Completion yields SUCCESS with any return values, or FAILED.

Communication Service forwards all responses to requester; request success/error endings shown. Command-specific result fields required only in final successful response and optional otherwise per figure note.

conditions_timers_and_modal_rules: Queueing is conditional on component support; no universal queue required.
Initial, periodic and stale-command timers have separate purposes.
Some commands need no authorization, but this flow does not enumerate exemptions.
source_described_state_and_registry_effe: Protocol states queued/in progress/final outcome, not automatically measured physical result.
limits_and_distinctions: Illustrative function flow is not an implementation/state-machine conformance test.
No automatic retry, rollback, cancellation, queue discipline or physical safety behavior inferred.
Do not conflate response reference with Request.request id; saved ambiguity remains.

figure_observation.caption: Figure 29 - Command Execution by ISA Component

nested_flows.title: Command Authorization
nested_flows.source_span_text:
6.3.3.8.2   Command Authorization
When authorization of a command is necessary, the Communication Service requests the
Authorization Service to determine if the requesting component is authorized to request
the execution of the command by the performing component. There are a small number of
commands for which authorization is not necessary.


Figure 30 - Command Authorization
nested_flows.trigger_or_entry: Authorization needed for a requested command by requesting component against performing component.

ordered_exchange_and_branches.description: Communication Service Check Authorization of Command receives Request, sends Request to Authorization Service with diagram label command=Authorize, header & message=received Request message.
Authorization Service Determine Authorization of Request returns authorized=yes/type=SUCCESS if permitted, authorized=no/type=SUCCESS if denied, or type=FAILED if unable to perform authorization.
Communication Service obtains decision and returns to its calling flow.

conditions_timers_and_modal_rules: A small number of commands do not require authorization; no names are supplied in this block.
source_described_state_and_registry_effe: Authorization decision, not command execution.
limits_and_distinctions: A successful decision service invocation can return denial.
Do not rename diagram Authorize to DMS Authorize Request silently, or equate subject with requester.
No identity/credential/policy implementation invented.

nested_flows.title: Graceful Deregistration
nested_flows.source_span_text:
6.3.3.9     Graceful Deregistration
An ISA component must request deregistration when it intends to leave the ISA network to
which it is joined (e.g., prior to shutdown).




                                                                                          53
 Figure 31 - Graceful Deregistration
nested_flows.trigger_or_entry: Component intends to leave network, e.g. before shutdown; prose says must request deregistration.

ordered_exchange_and_branches.description: Operational registrant sends Registration source=Registrant UCI/opcode=REQUEST REMOVE.
Communication Service Deregister Component returns Registration labelled type=REMOVED and announces Administrative about=Registrant UCI/opcode=DEVICE REMOVED (literal figure labels).
Registrant can keep connection open and end Deregistered, or Terminate Connection and become Disconnected.
Live Data Service sends Administrative to subscribed delivery, removes UCI registry record and removes any subscriptions for UCI from Subscription Table.

conditions_timers_and_modal_rules: Subscription Removal prose separately requires subscriber remove subscription before requesting deregistration.
Connection closure is an explicit choice in this graceful flow, unlike forced-timeout flows.
source_described_state_and_registry_effe: Logical membership removed; cache/subscription cleanup.

Keep figure type/opcode labels visible against DMS Registration.opcode and Administrative.code.
No historical data deletion or physical shutdown performed.

nested_flows.source_span_text:
6.3.3.10.1 Virtual ISA Component Joining
If a virtual ISA component has become available to the CIC, the CIC announces the
availability of the component and submits a configuration and status report for it.




                                                                                        54
 Figure 32 - Virtual ISA Component Joining




                                            55
nested_flows.trigger_or_entry: Virtual component becomes available to CIC; communication is occurring between composition member and CIC.

ordered_exchange_and_branches.description: Virtual member Communicate with CIC provides capabilities and status to CIC Communicate with Subcomponents.
CIC Mediate Between Non-ISA Data Model and ISA Data Model prepares Administrative, Config and Status representations.

CIC Announce Subcomponents emits Administrative about=Subcomponent UCI/code=DEVICE ADDED; Declare Capabilities emits Config source=Subcomponent UCI with declarations/states; Report Status emits Status source=Subcomponent UCI and subcomponent property values.
Communication Service routes all three messages to Live Data Service.
Live Data Service creates registry record for Subcomponent UCI, adds Config and Status contents to that record and invokes subscribed-to delivery.

conditions_timers_and_modal_rules: Figure is a CIC mediation scenario and does not depict a separate direct virtual-component transport connection/registration handshake.
source_described_state_and_registry_effe: Virtual component becomes network-visible through CIC reports; distinct source/about identity preserved.
limits_and_distinctions: No physical containment, hardware identity taxonomy or direct ISA protocol support by member inferred.
Do not treat CIC transport sender as automatically the producer UCI in payload.
No generic format-conversion algorithm or proven lossless mediation supplied.

6.3.3.10.2 Virtual ISA Component Leaving
If a virtual ISA component becomes unavailable to the CIC, the CIC announces the loss of
availability of the component.


Figure 33 - Virtual ISA Component Leaving




                                                                                           56
nested_flows.trigger_or_entry: Communication has stopped between subcomponent and CIC; virtual component unavailable to CIC.

ordered_exchange_and_branches.description: CIC Communicate with Subcomponents observes unavailable subcomponent and mediates non-ISA data into Administrative message.
CIC Announce Subcomponents sends Administrative about=Subcomponent UCI/code=DEVICE REMOVED.
Communication Service routes notification to Live Data Service, which deletes registry record for Subcomponent UCI and invokes subscribed-to delivery.

conditions_timers_and_modal_rules: Availability loss is relative to CIC communication; no direct Registration REQUEST REMOVE exchange is drawn.
source_described_state_and_registry_effe: Logical registry visibility removed.
limits_and_distinctions: No proof physical device was removed/destroyed, CIC disconnected or historic data deleted.

nested_flows.title: Observation Publication for Virtual ISA Component
nested_flows.source_span_text:
6.3.3.10.3 Observation Publication for Virtual ISA Component
If an ISA component plays the role of a CIC for a virtual ISA component, and the virtual ISA
component produces observables, the CIC publishes observables to the ISA Controller on
behalf of the virtual ISA component.


Figure 34 - Observation Publication for Virtual ISA Component




                                                                                           57
nested_flows.trigger_or_entry: Virtual component produces observables; CIC publishes on its behalf.

ordered_exchange_and_branches.description: Producer Communicate with CIC passes observation information to CIC Communicate with Subcomponents.
CIC mediates between non-ISA and ISA data models to form Event, then Publish Observation sends Event with source=Producer UCI and one or more observables declared for Producer.
Communication Service routes Event to Live Data Service, which invokes subscribed-to delivery.

conditions_timers_and_modal_rules: Producer and publisher are separately labelled actors; source UCI names producer even though CIC publishes.
source_described_state_and_registry_effe: Mediated Event publication attributed to virtual producer.
limits_and_distinctions: Do not collapse transport sender, publisher/CIC, event source/producer, physical detector and observing system.
No new physical device, duplicate observation or original resultTime created by message mediation.
No Event caching/archival behavior shown.

source_wording_notes.subject: Authorization command and parameter naming
source_wording_notes.source_as_seen: Figures 8 and 30 both label command = Authorize and header & message = received Registration/Request message.
source_wording_notes.saved_comparison: DMS173 Authorize Registration requires client/server and optional registration; DMS174 Authorize Request requires subject/request. No generic Authorize command exists among the 96 saved command entries.
source_wording_notes.treatment: Preserve SDD wording as diagram vocabulary and link semantically to the distinct DMS contracts. No invented alias or wire compatibility. Both true and false authorization outcomes can accompany SUCCESS; inability is FAILED.

source_wording_notes.subject: Initial Status receipt timer starting point

source_wording_notes.treatment: Retain both timing statements, no guessed reconciliation or installed numeric interval. Figure 17 uses Initial Status Receipt Timer, without resolving start-point wording.

source_wording_notes.subject: Config and Status content scope
source_wording_notes.source_as_seen: Initial Status prose says all declared property values; Figure 16 narrows to declared properties ready and being reported. Config-change figures send whole CCD when declarations change and changed ready/reporting states plus Status changes.
source_wording_notes.saved_comparison: DMS Config optional CCD and distinct state lists; Status property list; Get Status215 retrieves declared-ready values even if reporting disabled.
source_wording_notes.treatment: Keep message publication scope distinct from explicit Get Status selection, and whole CCD replacement distinct from state/value deltas. No claim all possible properties or capabilities are present.

source_wording_notes.subject: Service recommendation is optional and shown path not exhaustive
source_wording_notes.source_as_seen: Figure15 says neither requesting nor using recommended services is required; positive-provider path follows initial Status.
source_wording_notes.saved_comparison: DMS238/240 service parameter optional; omission means no acceptable provider currently available.
source_wording_notes.treatment: Positive-provider diagram does not remove full DMS omission semantics or force chosen-provider use.

source_wording_notes.subject: Renewal versus revival wording
source_wording_notes.source_as_seen: Figure10 RENEW redirects to Registration. Figure20 NON RESPONSIVE requests Status and returns REVIVED plus Config refresh. §6.3.3.4.6 prose says registration renewal request, while Figure21 shows NON RESPONSIVE and Revival Status Receipt Timer.
source_wording_notes.saved_comparison: DMS353 distinguishes RENEW, NON RESPONSIVE and REVIVED operations explicitly.
source_wording_notes.treatment: Record local prose/figure mismatch; keep flows and operations distinct. Do not silently rewrite source or treat revival as full re-registration.

source_wording_notes.subject: Discover diagram names/response representation differ from DMS
source_wording_notes.source_as_seen: Figure22 uses script input, ucis return, and separately drawn Config/Status addressed to requester.

source_wording_notes.treatment: Preserve both representations. Do not create script/ucis aliases, remove include ucis, or assert an alternative wire encoding from schematic arrows.

source_wording_notes.subject: Subscription key-content scenarios versus complete query contract
source_wording_notes.source_as_seen: Figure23 shows Add Subscription query and assigned ID plus initial matching Config/Status; Figure25 shows body=matched message for four categories.
source_wording_notes.saved_comparison: DMS162 supports optional name/consumer and name replacement; DMS478 ID has creator/consumer/name; DQL2.4 without cache suppresses initial cached values; query select clauses can project fields.
source_wording_notes.treatment: No contradiction merely because schematic omits optional fields. Preserve projection, cache choice and distinct creator/consumer. Four subscription message kinds do not expand to entire seven-message union.

source_wording_notes.subject: Removal function retains generic subscription label
source_wording_notes.source_as_seen: Figure24 is Subscription Removal and Request is Remove Subscription, but subscriber function box says Subscribe to Messages.
source_wording_notes.treatment: Retain literal figure label; interpret scenario by actual Remove Subscription exchange and caption. Not a new command or correction to source.

source_wording_notes.subject: Publication examples versus Event payload cardinality
source_wording_notes.source_as_seen: Figures26 and34 say one or more declared observables in publication Event.
source_wording_notes.saved_comparison: DMS306 Event observable list is Required0+; this permits empty collection in the general type.
source_wording_notes.treatment: Source-defined publication scenario is narrower than generic envelope. Do not change native datatype cardinality. No actual observation or physical effect proven.

source_wording_notes.subject: SER and Event Reference are not silently equated
source_wording_notes.source_as_seen: Update/recall prose names Shared Event Reference (SER); figures use ser=ID of prior Event message.
source_wording_notes.saved_comparison: DMS306 names event reference; DMS382 Event Reference requires creator UCI, Event ID and original event time. DMS156 Recall is String reason for recalling referenced Event.
source_wording_notes.treatment: Preserve SER source wording and semantic prior-event relationship without assuming bare message identifier, Event ID or Event Reference are equivalent. Update advises replacement only for updated observables; recall advises cease use of all prior observables; neither proves deletion or compliance.

source_wording_notes.subject: Execution diagram outcomes and timer scope
source_wording_notes.source_as_seen: Figure29 lists validation/busy response alternatives and FAILED on stale timer expiry. It distinguishes initial/periodic/stale timers and queued/in-progress/final responses.
source_wording_notes.saved_comparison: DMS456 additionally explicitly defines INSUFFICIENT TIME for no execution attempt when completion by stale time cannot be achieved.
source_wording_notes.treatment: Do not treat illustrative Figure29 outcome labels as an exhaustive enum or silently change its labels. Do not conflate pre-execution insufficient-time refusal with failure after deadline expiry. Full native response contract preserved.

source_wording_notes.subject: Graceful removal type/opcode labels
source_wording_notes.source_as_seen: Figure31 labels Registration reply type=REMOVED and Administrative notification opcode=DEVICE REMOVED.
source_wording_notes.saved_comparison: DMS307 Registration uses opcode; DMS304 Administrative uses code. Other SDD removal figures generally use those names.
source_wording_notes.treatment: Retain literal mismatched labels in evidence, link to appropriate DMS structures without changing source or claiming alternate fields exist.

source_wording_notes.subject: Virtual component identity versus CIC routing and physical organization
source_wording_notes.source_as_seen: CIC mediates virtual member capabilities/status and observations. Administrative.about names subcomponent; Config/Status.source name subcomponent; virtual-observation Event.source names producer while CIC is publisher.
source_wording_notes.saved_comparison: Header from/to routing is distinct from message source; previous S06-R006 architectural reconciliation remains open.
source_wording_notes.treatment: Use as participation/mediation evidence, not physical taxonomy or blanket equality between original author, sender, publisher and detector. Retain distinction and forward to broader architecture reconciliation.

source_wording_notes.subject: Registration ADD shorthand in connection timer annotation
source_wording_notes.source_as_seen: Figure7 Registration Receipt Timer annotation says receiving Registration ADD message after IPL Handshake Complete; Figure8 registrant request says opcode=REQUEST ADD.
source_wording_notes.saved_comparison: DMS353 Registration Operation includes REQUEST ADD and ADDED, not a separate ADD variant.
source_wording_notes.treatment: Retain literal ADD annotation as source shorthand/wording without inventing an ADD operation, alias or corrected source label.

source_wording_notes.source_wording: Table5 places entry to Operational at receipt of the Controller initial Config; Figure5 uses the received initial Config transition. Figure16 reaches its Operational endpoint after the registrant receives initial Status.
source_wording_notes.handling: Preserve both source timings explicitly. Section6.3.3 says the diagrams indicate phase transitions; do not invent a single reconciled onset condition or silently replace either statement.
