records.source_span_text:
1.2       Terminology
 There are a number of terms used in describing ISA that should be understood prior to
 reading this document. Terms, with a brief explanation, are provided below:


 Table 2 - Terminology

  Term                      Description


  Command                   A task that an ISA component can perform upon request.


  Component Capability      The set of declarations of the ISA capabilities supported by an ISA
  Description (CCD)         component.




                                                                                                  1
 Term                   Description


Configuration set      The combination of a CCD and the ready and reporting states of the ISA
                       capabilities declared in the CCD.


Core ISA service       A service that must be available with any ISA deployment in order to reach
                       full capability.


Historical data        Information, data, and notifications that were generated in the past.


ISA capability         A property, observable, or command declared by an ISA component.


ISA component          A component that complies with the ISA interface and supports the required
                       ISA behaviors.


ISA controller         A collection of core ISA services acting as a single unit to provide ISA
                       functionality. An ISA Controller comprises a single instance of each core ISA
                       service.


ISA interface          The combination of communication protocols, security technologies, data
                       encodings, and messages defined for ISA.


ISA network            A set of interconnected ISA components.


ISA service            A service defined for ISA, including core and optional services.


Observable             Information that a component can publish about observations that it makes.


Optional ISA service   A service that may be available with an ISA deployment but is not
                       guaranteed to be present.


Property               Information that a component can report about its current status.


Service                A self-contained collection of related capabilities and behaviors that
                       supports a specified interface.




                                                                                                       2

records.title: Fundamental ISA Component Requirements
records.source_span_text:
4.0 Fundamental ISA Component Requirements
 This section contains the requirements for functionality that pertains to all ISA
 components, with the exception of the requirements for providing optional ISA services,
 which are presented in the subsequent sections. The section is organized to follow the
 lifecycle for participation in an ISA network.

 For certain topics, the requirements are grouped into a Client-Side Behavior subsection and
 a General Behavior subsection. This is the case for topics for which there are both
 requirements specific to the behavior of an ISA component when it is playing the client-
 side role for a connection and requirements that are independent of connection role. A
 component is said to be playing a client-side role for a connection when it initiated the
 connection.

[CMPT-L-0001] Unique UCI

The ISA component UCI shall be unique.

Parent Requirements:

         [CMPT-M-0001] Valid UCI

[CMPT-L-0002] UCI Length

The ISA component UCI shall have a length of at least one letter.

Note: A single digit or hyphen is not acceptable; it must contain at least one letter.

Parent Requirements:

         [CMPT-M-0001] Valid UCI

[CMPT-L-0003] Acceptable UCI Characters

The ISA component UCI shall consist of only letters, digits, hyphens, and plus signs (+).

Note: Refer to requirements CMPT-L-0007 and CMPT-L-0008 for rules on the use of plus signs (+).

Parent Requirements:

         [CMPT-M-0001] Valid UCI

[CMPT-L-0004] First UCI Character

The ISA component UCI shall begin with a letter.

Parent Requirements:

         [CMPT-M-0001] Valid UCI




                                                                                                  8
 [CMPT-L-0005] Last UCI Character

The ISA component UCI shall end with a letter or digit.

Parent Requirements:

        [CMPT-M-0001] Valid UCI

[CMPT-L-0006] Prohibited UCI Character Combination

The ISA component UCI shall only contain non-consecutive hyphens.

Parent Requirements:

        [CMPT-M-0001] Valid UCI

[CMPT-L-0007] Reserved UCI Character

The ISA component UCI shall only contain a plus sign (+) when used for a virtual ISA component.

Note: The plus sign (+) is used as a special character to assign unique UCIs to virtual ISA components based on
the UCI of the supporting ISA component.

Parent Requirements:

        [CMPT-M-0001] Valid UCI

[CMPT-L-0008] Virtual Component Identification

If an ISA component supports virtual ISA components, the ISA component shall use a UCI for the
virtual ISA component that is composed of the ISA component’s own UCI, followed by a plus sign
(+), followed by an identifier that is unique within the set of virtual ISA components supported by
the ISA component.

Note: If the ISA component is “foo,” the virtual ISA component would be assigned a UCI such as “foo+bar” or
“foo+A00012.”

Parent Requirements:

        [CMPT-M-0001] Valid UCI

native_requirements.source_requirement_text:
[CMPT-L-0008] Virtual Component Identification

If an ISA component supports virtual ISA components, the ISA component shall use a UCI for the
virtual ISA component that is composed of the ISA component’s own UCI, followed by a plus sign
(+), followed by an identifier that is unique within the set of virtual ISA components supported by
the ISA component.

Note: If the ISA component is “foo,” the virtual ISA component would be assigned a UCI such as “foo+bar” or
“foo+A00012.”

Parent Requirements:

        [CMPT-M-0001] Valid UCI

records.meaning: Eighteen native requirements distinguish required capability support, two recommended properties, conditional command support and per-property command applicability.
native_rules: Retain H0003,M0007–M0009,L0017–L0030 and their exact modalities/conditions.
Identity and Operating State are should recommendations; Maximum/Minimum Status Interval are shall requirements.
Set Observable Reporting is conditional on publishing observables; Set Property is conditional on settable properties.
Get Property execution is supported for every declared property; Set Property execution is scoped to every declared settable property.
limitations: The DMS Required2-property/7-command and Recommended2-property/2-command bins stay intact; source-specific conditional wording is added without silently harmonizing the sources.
Supporting a command is distinct from a permitted request, successful execution, actual property value or physical effect.
The READ WRITE explanatory Note does not replace the full saved mutability vocabulary.

records.title: Synchronizing Time
records.source_span_text:
4.2.1       Synchronizing Time
[CMPT-H-0004] Synchronizing Time

The ISA component shall have accurate time synchronized with Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).

        [CMPT-M-0010] Synchronize to an NTP source.

4.2.2       Discovering Controllers
[CMPT-H-0005] Discovering Controllers

The ISA component shall be able to identify ISA Controllers to which to connect.

Child Requirements:

        [CMPT-M-0011] Auto-Detect Controllers
        [CMPT-M-0012] Configurable Connections

[CMPT-M-0011] Auto-Detect Controllers

The ISA component should support detection of available ISA Controllers residing on the local area
network.

Note: Network configurations might severely limit the use of multicast when used as the ISA Controller detection
method.

Parent Requirements:

        [CMPT-H-0005] Discovering Controllers

Child Requirements:

        [CMPT-L-0033] Dynamic Connection Configuration

[CMPT-M-0012] Configurable Connections

The ISA component should support configurable address and port parameters for connecting to an
ISA Controller.

Parent Requirements:

        [CMPT-H-0005] Discovering Controllers

Child Requirements:

        [CMPT-L-0034] Static Connection Configuration

[CMPT-L-0033] Dynamic Connection Configuration

When the use of a dynamic mechanism for locating ISA Controllers is enabled, the ISA component
shall use mDNS to obtain network information for Controllers.




                                                                                                              18
 Note: The ISA Controllers are identified using the following service identifier: _isa._tcp.

Parent Requirements:

         [CMPT-M-0011] Auto-Detect Controllers

[CMPT-L-0034] Static Connection Configuration

When the use of a dynamic mechanism for locating ISA Controllers is disabled, the ISA component
shall obtain network information for the Controllers from the component’s local configuration.

Parent Requirements:

         [CMPT-M-0012] Configurable Connections
records.source_locator: ISA Component Requirements 6.0r4 (31 October 2023), §4.2.2 Discovering Controllers; PDF pages 25,26; printed pages 18,19

records.meaning: Controller identification supports recommended automatic/local-network and configurable-endpoint approaches, with conditional mDNS versus local-configuration requirements.
native_rules: Identification capability is a shall; automatic local-network detection and configurable address/port support are should recommendations.
If dynamic location is enabled, use mDNS and the _isa._tcp service identifier.
If dynamic location is disabled, use local component configuration for Controller network information.
The source warns that network configuration may severely limit multicast-based detection.
limitations: Dynamic discovery is not unconditional; no fixed address, port, multicast reachability, successful detection or endpoint-selection algorithm is supplied.
Endpoint discovery differs from DMS Discover for component/message information, and neither establishes physical equipment identity.
The source does not prescribe an external registry, a configuration file schema or communication topology.

records.title: Connecting
records.source_span_text:
4.3.1       Connecting
[CMPT-H-0006] Connecting

The ISA component shall be able to establish secure connections.

Child Requirements:

         [CMPT-M-0013] Initiate Connection
         [CMPT-M-0014] Secure Connections

4.3.1.1 Client-Side Behavior
[CMPT-M-0013] Initiate Connection

Upon startup, when a connection to an ISA Controller is needed, the ISA component shall initiate a
secure connection with an ISA Controller.

Note: For ISA components that are not ISA Controllers, a connection to an ISA Controller will always be needed
at startup. For ISA Controllers, a connection to another ISA Controller may or may not be needed at startup.

Parent Requirements:

         [CMPT-H-0006] Connecting




                                                                                                                 19
 Child Requirements:

        [CMPT-L-0035] Determine Connection Need
        [CMPT-L-0036] Initiate Connection Upon Need
        [CMPT-L-0037] Connection Attempt Frequency

[CMPT-L-0035] Determine Connection Need

Upon startup, the ISA component shall determine if a connection to an ISA Controller is needed.

Parent Requirements:

        [CMPT-M-0013] Initiate Connection

[CMPT-L-0036] Initiate Connection Upon Need

When a connection to an ISA Controller is needed, the ISA component shall send a connection
request to the selected ISA Controller, using the network information for the Controller.

Note: Selection of the ISA Controller could be based on dynamically obtained or static network information and
could follow any selection logic that is appropriate for the component.

Parent Requirements:

        [CMPT-M-0013] Initiate Connection

[CMPT-L-0037] Connection Attempt Frequency

The ISA component shall attempt to connect to an ISA Controller no more frequently than every 5
seconds.

Parent Requirements:

        [CMPT-M-0013] Initiate Connection


4.3.1.2 General Behavior
[CMPT-M-0014] Secure Connections

The ISA component shall establish secure connections using the digital certificate under possession.

Parent Requirements:

        [CMPT-H-0006] Connecting

Child Requirements:

        [CMPT-L-0038] TCP with TLS



                                                                                                                 20
 [CMPT-L-0038] TCP with TLS

If using Transmission Control Protocol (TCP), the ISA component shall use Transport Layer Security
(TLS) to secure the connection.

Note: Use the certificate assigned to the ISA component for encrypting the connection.

Parent Requirements:

        [CMPT-M-0014] Secure Connections
records.source_locator: ISA Component Requirements 6.0r4 (31 October 2023), §4.3.1 Connecting; PDF pages 26,27,28; printed pages 19,20,21
records.source_span_hash_basis: Exact provided nonoverlapping UTF-8 registered span from cmpt_layout.txt, with original labels, spelling, notes and page breaks preserved.
records.meaning: Connection requirements separate startup need, endpoint selection, attempt cadence and certificate/TLS usage, with client-side and general behavior identified.
native_rules: Determine startup need and initiate a secure Controller connection when needed. Non-Controllers always need it at startup; Controllers may or may not need a connection to another Controller.
Use the selected Controller’s dynamic or static network information; selection logic is left to what is appropriate for the component.
Attempt connections no more frequently than every five seconds.
Use the possessed digital certificate for secure connections; if TCP is used, secure it with TLS using the assigned certificate as noted.
limitations: No fixed endpoint selection, exact periodic retry schedule, retry count, backoff formula or success guarantee is supplied.
Client-side behavior is a connection responsibility, not a disjoint physical equipment class; general certificate behavior does not establish authorization.
CMPT-L-0038 is conditional and names no TLS version. The previously reviewed ICD TLS 1.2 rule remains separately attributed to its edition.
No connection, certificate installation, validation operation or current security recommendation is claimed.

records.source_span_text:
4.3.2       Establishing Format
[CMPT-H-0007] Establishing Format

The ISA component shall negotiate the presentation format to be used for message exchange over a
connection.

Child Requirements:

        [CMPT-M-0015] Negotiate Format

        [CMPT-M-0017] IPL Usage


4.3.2.1 Client-Side Behavior
[CMPT-M-0015] Negotiate Format

Upon connecting with an ISA Controller, the ISA component shall initiate negotiation of a
compatible ISA Presentation Layer (IPL) format with the Controller.

Note: Sensor CE will be using IPL format 3, which is Google Protocol Buffers using the ISA Static Data Model.

Parent Requirements:

        [CMPT-H-0007] Establishing Format

Child Requirements:

        [CMPT-L-0041] Send IPL Handshake Begin
        [CMPT-L-0042] Indicate Supported IPL Formats
        [CMPT-L-0043] Sort Supported IPL Formats
        [CMPT-L-0169] Encapsulate ISA Envelope
        [CMPT-L-0045] Enter Application Data Exchange
        [CMPT-L-0046] Handle Unexpected Application Data




                                                                                                                21
 [CMPT-L-0041] Send IPL Handshake Begin

Upon establishing a connection to an ISA Controller, the ISA component shall send the IPL
Handshake Begin message to the Controller.

Parent Requirements:

       [CMPT-M-0015] Negotiate Format

[CMPT-L-0042] Indicate Supported IPL Formats

When generating the IPL Handshake Begin message, the ISA component shall list all of the IPL
formats defined in the ISA Interface Control Document that are supported by the ISA component.

Parent Requirements:

       [CMPT-M-0015] Negotiate Format

[CMPT-L-0043] Sort Supported IPL Formats

When generating the IPL Handshake Begin message, the ISA component shall list the supported IPL
formats in order of preference, with the most-preferred format listed first.

Parent Requirements:

       [CMPT-M-0015] Negotiate Format

[CMPT-L-0169] Encapsulate ISA Envelope

When sending an ISA envelope, the ISA component shall encapsulate the ISA envelope in an IPL
Application Data message.

Parent Requirements:

       [CMPT-M-0015] Negotiate Format

[CMPT-L-0045] Enter Application Data Exchange

Upon receiving an IPL Handshake Complete message, the ISA component may begin exchanging IPL
Application Data messages.

Parent Requirements:

       [CMPT-M-0015] Negotiate Format




                                                                                                 22
 [CMPT-L-0046] Handle Unexpected Application Data

When an IPL Application Data message is received before the IPL Handshake Complete message,
the ISA component shall send an IPL Error message containing the 0x04 error code to the IPL
message sender.

Parent Requirements:

       [CMPT-M-0015] Negotiate Format

4.3.2.2 General Behavior
[CMPT-M-0017] IPL Usage

When exchanging messages, the ISA component shall use the negotiated IPL format.

Parent Requirements:

       [CMPT-H-0007] Establishing Format

Child Requirements:

       [CMPT-L-0047] Use Negotiated IPL Format

       [CMPT-L-0051] Generate IPL Error on Invalid Message
       [CMPT-L-0052] Generate Error on Decode Failure
       [CMPT-L-0053] IPL Message Length

Use the smallest fitting Application Data wrapper; set the first byte to IPL specification version and the second to IPL message type; create the proper message length.

CMPT supplies shall responses for its explicit error conditions; broader ICD can/may descriptions remain unchanged and do not imply automatic disconnection.
The single may in L-0045 allows exchange; it does not require an immediate data transmission or complete registration.
No execution, decoding test, negotiated connection, wire-field DIM class or schema conformance is asserted.

records.source_span_text:
4.3.3      Registering
All of the requirements in this section pertain to client-side behavior. Server-side behavior
for registration are specific to an ISA Controller.

[CMPT-H-0008] Registering

The ISA component shall be able to register its identity with the ISA network.

Child Requirements:

        [CMPT-M-0018] Make Registration Request
        [CMPT-M-0019] Registration Completion Time Constraint

[CMPT-M-0018] Make Registration Request

Upon successfully negotiating an ISA IPL format with an ISA Controller, the ISA component shall
send a registration request to the Controller.

Note: An ISA component has reached the connected state upon successfully negotiating an ISA IPL format.

Parent Requirements:

        [CMPT-H-0008] Registering

Child Requirements:

        [CMPT-L-0054] Use REQUEST ADD to Register

[CMPT-M-0019] Registration Completion Time Constraint

The ISA component shall send a registration request to the ISA Controller within 30 seconds of
successfully negotiating an ISA IPL format with the Controller.

Parent Requirements:

        [CMPT-H-0008] Registering

Child Requirements:

        [CMPT-L-0055] Registration Completion Time

[CMPT-L-0054] Use REQUEST ADD to Register

Upon receiving an IPL Handshake Complete message from the ISA Controller, the ISA component
shall send a Registration message containing the REQUEST ADD code to the Controller.




                                                                                                          25
 Parent Requirements:

        [CMPT-M-0018] Make Registration Request

[CMPT-L-0055] Registration Completion Time

The ISA component shall send a Registration message containing the REQUEST ADD code to the ISA
Controller within 30 seconds of establishing a connection to the Controller.

Parent Requirements:

        [CMPT-M-0019] Registration Completion Time Constrain

native_rules: All requirements in this section are client-side; server-side registration behavior is specific to a Controller.
Send a registration request upon successful IPL-format negotiation; the note calls that the connected state.
M-0019 requires sending the request within thirty seconds after successful format negotiation.
L-0054 sends Registration REQUEST ADD upon Handshake Complete; L-0055 sets thirty seconds from establishing a connection.
limitations: Sending REQUEST ADD is not ADDED, successful joining, task authorization or acceptance of identity.
Completion in the titles does not change the operative requirement from sending the request to completing registration.
Connection/negotiation terminology and the two timing anchors remain source-qualified; no equivalence, priority rule, extra timeout or sixty-second timer is invented.
Full DMS Registration fields and operation enum remain unchanged. The later lifecycle/registration handling clauses retain their separate assigned scope.

[CMPT-L-0058] Include CCD in Initial Config Message

When sending an initial Config message, the ISA component shall include its CCD and all capability
state values equal to false in the message.

Notes: 1) an initial Config message occurs when a component joins, re-joins, responds to a Registration message
containing the NON RESPONSIVE code, or responds to a Get Config command. 2) "all capability state values
equal to false" means any ready or reporting state (property, observable, or command) with a value of false.

Parent Requirements:

[CMPT-L-0059] Publish Update Config Message

Upon change to an ISA component’s configuration, the ISA component shall send an update Config
message to the connected-to ISA controller.

Note: an update Config message occurs when any property, observable, or command state (ready or reporting)
changes.

Parent Requirements:

        [CMPT-M-0028] Publish Configuration Update




                                                                                                              31
 [CMPT-L-0060] Update Config Message Completion Time Constraint

The ISA component shall send the update Config message within 30 seconds of a configuration
change occurring.

Parent Requirements:

[CMPT-L-0061] Include CCD in Update Config Message

When sending an update Config message, if the configuration set change includes one or more
capability declaration changes, the ISA component shall include its entire CCD in the message.

Parent Requirements:

        [CMPT-M-0030] Publish Changes in Configuration Update

[CMPT-L-0062] Include All Capability State Changes in Update Config Message

When sending an update Config message, if the configuration set change includes one or more
capability state changes, the ISA component shall include all capability state values equal to false in
the message.

Note: This means that a component wanting to indicate that all property states are now true would send a
Config message with an empty property state list (and similarly for observable or command states).

Parent Requirements:

        [CMPT-M-0030] Publish Changes in Configuration Update

[CMPT-L-0064] Declare Supported Commands

When including a CCD in a Config message, the ISA component shall include declarations for all
supported commands in the CCD.

        [CMPT-M-0022] Declare Supported Commands in Initial Configuration

        [CMPT-M-0030] Publish Changes in Configuration Update

[CMPT-L-0065] Commands Conform to Specification

component shall conform to the ISA DMS in its declaration.

supported observables in the CCD.

[CMPT-L-0069] Observables Conform to Specification

For each observable declared by an ISA component that is specified in the ISA DMS, the ISA
component shall conform to the ISA DMS in its declaration.

Parent Requirements:

       [CMPT-M-0024] Declare Supported Observables in Initial Configuration

 [CMPT-L-0070] Declare Supported Custom Data Structures

supported custom data structures.

[CMPT-L-0072] Commands Ready Set to True

For each declared command that is ready to be executed, the ISA component shall maintain a ready
state of true.

Note: A command is considered to be ready when execution of the command has been enabled. Readiness does
not connote availability, as a command could be enabled but the component could be too busy with other tasks
to execute the command.

Parent Requirements:

        [CMPT-M-0026] Indicate Ready States in Initial Configuration

[CMPT-L-0073] Commands Not Ready Set to False

For each declared command that is not ready to be executed, the ISA component shall maintain a
ready state of false.

Note: A command is considered to be not ready when execution of the command has been disabled.

Parent Requirements:

        [CMPT-M-0026] Indicate Ready States in Initial Configuration




                                                                                                               34
 [CMPT-L-0074] Properties Ready Set to True

For each declared property that is ready to be provided, the ISA component shall maintain a ready
state of true.

Note: A property is considered to be ready when the value of the property is maintained by the component.
Readiness connotes data accessibility upon request, but does not connote inclusion in status reports (via Status
messages) or observation reports (via Event messages). Report inclusion is governed by the reporting state of the
property.

Parent Requirements:

        [CMPT-M-0026] Indicate Ready States in Initial Configuration

[CMPT-L-0075] Properties Not Ready Set to False

For each declared property that is not ready to be provided, the ISA component shall maintain a
ready state of false.

Note: A property is considered to be not ready when the value of the property is not maintained by the
component.

Parent Requirements:

        [CMPT-M-0026] Indicate Ready States in Initial Configuration

[CMPT-L-0076] Properties Reporting Set to True

For each declared property that has a ready state of true and is to be reported, the ISA component
shall maintain a reporting state of true.

Note: A property that is to be reported is included in the relevant status reports (via Status messages) and
potentially in Event messages.

Parent Requirements:

        [CMPT-M-0027] Indicate Reporting States in Initial Configuration

[CMPT-L-0077] Properties Not Reporting Set to False

For each declared property that has a ready state of true and is not to be reported, the ISA
component shall maintain a reporting state of false.

Parent Requirements:

        [CMPT-M-0027] Indicate Reporting States in Initial Configuration




                                                                                                               35
 [CMPT-L-0078] Observables Ready Set to True

If an ISA component publishes observables, for each declared observable that is ready to be
provided, the ISA component shall maintain a ready state of true.

Note: An observable is considered to be ready when recording of the value of the observable has been enabled.
Readiness does not connote inclusion in observation reports (via Event messages). The latter is governed by the
reporting state of the observable.

Parent Requirements:

        [CMPT-M-0026] Indicate Ready States in Initial Configuration

[CMPT-L-0079] Observables Not Ready Set to False

If an ISA component publishes observables, for each declared observable that is not ready to be
provided, the ISA component shall maintain a ready state of false.

Note: An observable is considered to be not ready when recording of the value of the observable has been
disabled.

Parent Requirements:

        [CMPT-M-0026] Indicate Ready States in Initial Configuration

[CMPT-L-0080] Observables Reporting Set to True

If an ISA component publishes observables, for each declared observable that has a ready state of
true and is to be reported, the ISA component shall maintain a reporting state of true.

Note: An observable that is to be reported is included in the relevant observation reports (via Event messages).

Parent Requirements:

        [CMPT-M-0027] Indicate Reporting States in Initial Configuration

[CMPT-L-0081] Observables Not Reporting Set to False

If an ISA component publishes observables, for each declared observable that has a ready state of
true and is not to be reported, the ISA component shall maintain a reporting state of false.

Note: An observable that is not to be reported is not included in the relevant observation reports (via Event
messages).

Parent Requirements:

        [CMPT-M-0027] Indicate Reporting States in Initial Configuration




                                                                                                                   36
 [CMPT-L-0082] Send Status Message Upon Configuration Update

Upon sending an update Config message that contains a CCD, the ISA component shall send a Status
message to the connected-to ISA controller, containing a value for every declared property for
which the reporting state is true.

Parent Requirements:

        [CMPT-M-0031] Send Status Upon Configuration Update

[CMPT-L-0170] Full Status Message Timing

The ISA component shall send the full Status message to the ISA Controller within 30 seconds of
sending the update Config message to the Controller.

Parent Requirements:

        [CMPT-M-0031] Send Status Upon Configuration Update

state values equal to false in the message.

4.3.5       Restricting Communications
[CMPT-H-0010] Restricting Communications

The ISA component shall limit communications until an operational state is reached.

Child Requirements:

        [CMPT-M-0032] Restricted Use of ISA Messages Until Operational

[CMPT-M-0032] Restricted Use of ISA Messages Until Operational

Prior to receiving an initial status from a connected-to ISA component, the ISA component shall not
send any ISA messages to the component other than those required to reach that point.

Note: An ISA component that initiated a connection to an ISA Controller has reached the operational state upon
receiving the ISA Controller’s initial status.

Parent Requirements:

        [CMPT-H-0010] Restricting Communications

Child Requirements:

        [CMPT-L-0083] Send No Request Messages Until Operational
        [CMPT-L-0084] Send No Event Messages Until Operational
        [CMPT-L-0085] Send No Administrative Messages Until Operational
        [CMPT-L-0086] Discard Early Request Message
        [CMPT-L-0087] Discard Early Event Message



                                                                                                             37
        [CMPT-L-0088] Discard Early Administrative Message

[CMPT-L-0083] Send No Request Messages Until Operational

The ISA component shall only send a Request message to a connected-to ISA component after
receiving an initial Status message from the component.

Parent Requirements:

       [CMPT-M-0032] Restricted Use of ISA Messages Until Operational

[CMPT-L-0084] Send No Event Messages Until Operational

The ISA component shall only send an Event message to a connected-to ISA component after
receiving an initial Status message from the component.

Parent Requirements:

       [CMPT-M-0032] Restricted Use of ISA Messages Until Operational

[CMPT-L-0085] Send No Administrative Messages Until Operational

The ISA component shall only send an Administrative message to a connected-to ISA component
after receiving an initial Status message from the component.

Parent Requirements:

       [CMPT-M-0032] Restricted Use of ISA Messages Until Operational

[CMPT-L-0086] Discard Early Request Message

If an ISA component receives a Request message from a connected-to ISA component prior to
receiving an initial Status message from the ISA component, the ISA component shall silently
discard the message.

Parent Requirements:

       [CMPT-M-0032] Restricted Use of ISA Messages Until Operational

[CMPT-L-0087] Discard Early Event Message

If an ISA component receives an Event message from a connected-to ISA component prior to
receiving an initial Status message from the ISA component, the ISA component shall silently
discard the message.

Parent Requirements:

       [CMPT-M-0032] Restricted Use of ISA Messages Until Operational



                                                                                               38
 [CMPT-L-0088] Discard Early Administrative Message

If an ISA component receives an Administrative message from a connected-to ISA component prior
to receiving an initial Status message from the ISA component, the ISA component shall silently
discard the message.

Parent Requirements:

        [CMPT-M-0032] Restricted Use of ISA Messages Until Operational

4.3.6       Reporting Status
[CMPT-H-0011] Reporting Status

The ISA component shall report its status to the ISA network.

4.3.6.1 Client-Side Behavior
[CMPT-M-0033] Send Initial Status

Upon sending an initial configuration to the ISA Controller, the ISA component shall send an initial
Status message to the Controller.

Note: An ISA component has reached the configured state upon receiving the ISA Controller’s initial
configuration.

Parent Requirements:

        [CMPT-H-0011] Reporting Status

        [CMPT-L-0089] Send Initial Status Message
        [CMPT-L-0090] Generate Initial Status Message

The ISA component shall send its initial Status message to the ISA Controller within 30 seconds of
sending an initial configuration to the Controller.

initial Status message to the Controller.

Parent Requirements:

native_rules: Sending initial Config triggers initialStatus to the Controller within30seconds; initialStatus includes every declared property with ready=true and reporting=true.
After initialStatus, periodicStatus transmission intervals are inclusively bounded by the component’s Minimum/MaximumStatusInterval property values.
A reporting-true property change triggers periodicStatus within500ms if no periodicStatus was sent within the current minimum interval; the source identifies the minimum/maximum window.

PeriodicStatus contains all and only declared properties changed since the lastStatus with ready=true and reporting=true. Never-reported properties count as changed; a property-appropriate delta is not numerically specified.
Changed Minimum/MaximumStatusInterval values apply to related behavior and computation of periodic intervals. The source note says these restrictions apply only to Status publication.
General periodic interval rules and the saved DMSthreshold publication regardless of interval remain both visible without an invented precedence algorithm.
limitations: 500ms is conditional change-to-send timing, not a default status interval, sampling period, unconditional latency or delivery guarantee.
No concrete minimum/maximum interval values, universal significant-change threshold, unit conversions or complete transition history are inferred.

All-and-only-changed selection is for periodic Status; initial and post-CCD-update full Status are separate contexts. DMS215 Get Status returns declared ready properties even if reporting is disabled, retaining its independent command-result selection.
Do not erase DMSthreshold publication regardless of status interval or invent a conflict-resolution algorithm among CMPT, DMS, ICD and SDDwording.
A Status heartbeat documents communication, not independently verified physical health or successful completion of work.
IPL3presence flags apply to list-valued Status/Event properties/observables as described, not to all lists or a generic readiness default.

native_text_by_page.3:
Executive Summary

The Integrated Sensor Architecture (ISA) is developed by the Army Program Executive
Officer for Intelligence, Electronic Warfare and Sensors (PEO IEW&S). The primary goal of
ISA is to enable systems to readily integrate into an existing network and dynamically share
data, information, and capabilities to help achieve situational awareness.

ISA is designed to make systems and their capabilities dynamically discoverable and
available to soldiers and platforms, without prior knowledge or specific integration, and
regardless of system type or ownership. This design maximizes access to useful data and
functionality, while minimizing integration complexity and lifecycle costs.

ISA is an interoperability solution designed to accomplish data, information, and capability
sharing within a tactical environment. ISA applies standards and technologies to address the
highly constrained communications, ever-changing conditions, and cybersecurity demands
that are characteristic of the tactical domain.

With the advent of the Army Common Operating Environment (COE) to eliminate the
capability shortfalls, cost overruns, and schedule delays that are common for system
acquisition, the Sensor Computing Environment (CE) was created to achieve sensor
interoperability across the Army’s tactical and enterprise realms. Specifically, Sensor CE is
defined to enable dynamic discovery of sensors, distribution of observation-related alerts,
dissemination of motion imagery, and control of sensors. Given ISA’s abilities and qualities,
ISA was chosen as the main material solution for Sensor CE.

source_wording_notes.source_literal: Event publication has a 500ms send bound after making the observation.
source_wording_notes.handling: Record this as a publication-latency obligation. It does not alter Event.time occurrence semantics or prove receipt/processing within 500ms.

source_wording_notes.source_literal: Observation update and recall use Event Reference; updates may include relevant observables not present in the previous Event, while recalls include Recall.
source_wording_notes.handling: Preserve lineage to the cited Event. Do not model update as a new unrelated event or recall as deletion of source history.

source_wording_notes.source_literal: On consuming an update, in-use observables from the cited Event are replaced as appropriate; on recall, use of the cited contents ceases. Notes say the treatment is usage/system specific.
source_wording_notes.handling: Do not invent universal database deletion, archival removal or immutable replacement behavior beyond the source's use semantics.

source_wording_notes.source_literal: A declared ready command is supported, but a valid request may still encounter temporary unavailability, queueing, BUSY, QUEUED or IN PROGRESS before final SUCCESS/FAILED.
source_wording_notes.handling: Keep readiness, immediate availability, queueing, response state, execution and achieved physical effect separate.

source_wording_notes.source_literal: Initial near-real-time command Response is due within 200ms; non-real-time initial Response is due within the performing component's Minimum Status Interval. Queued and long-running updates use the Minimum/Maximum Status Interval bounds.
source_wording_notes.handling: Retain the source-specific response timing and command classes; do not reinterpret the status-interval properties as only Status-message cadence or as execution completion deadlines.

source_wording_notes.source_literal: Commanding limits Requests to commands declared in the target CCD with ready state true and requires all needed input arguments.
source_wording_notes.handling: Treat declaration/readiness as request eligibility, not authorization, execution, success or physical-effect evidence.

source_wording_notes.source_literal: A virtual ISA component is an entity represented on the ISA network by another ISA component; DEVICE ADDED/REMOVED, Config, Status, Event and command behavior can all be emitted on its behalf.
source_wording_notes.handling: Model this as network representation/source attribution, not proof of physical containment, independent hardware identity, separate certificate or direct ISA interface.

source_wording_notes.source_literal: Virtual-command enablement may be implemented by execution on behalf of the virtual component, translation to a non-ISA message, or forwarding an ISA Request; these are examples in a Note.
source_wording_notes.handling: Keep mediation method separate from command semantics and do not infer a required transport or a permanent physical architecture from the examples.

source_wording_notes.source_literal: Disconnecting requires active subscriptions removed and deregistration requested; control-lock release is should. M0073 says should terminate the connection after Registration Removed, while L0168 says the component may close and notes the socket may remain open.
source_wording_notes.handling: Preserve deregistration and connection closure as separate steps and retain should/may wording rather than forcing a mandatory socket close.

source_wording_notes.source_literal: Appendix A defines Analysis, Demonstration, Inspection and Test, but its low-level requirement table contains165 mappings:145 Test and20 Inspection. CMPT-L-0164 is defined in §4.3.15 but absent from the table.
source_wording_notes.handling: Retain the Appendix as source conformance guidance and record the L0164 omission as a local source discrepancy. Do not assign an inferred verification method or turn verification method into runtime system data.

CNTR.visual_review_standing: Selected Appendix A and B pages visually inspected; no claim of all74 visually examined

final_candidate_qualifications.boundary: DEVICE REMOVED leads Live Data to discard retained Config/Status information for the cited participant; that is a service-visible state change, not proof of physical composition change or equipment destruction.

DEVICE REMOVED causes Live Data maintained Config/Status cleanup and subscription consumer cleanup; network/cache lifecycle is distinct from physical hardware removal or historical observation deletion.

An Event's detector-property values can cause a subscription to start or stop matching without themselves constituting a Status update, actual physical part change or original observation-result provenance.

Live Data caches new Config information only if sufficient computing resources exist, transmits maintained matching Config on subscription creation and removes maintained Config on DEVICE REMOVED. This is not original source-history erasure.

Live Data maintains new Status information only if resources permit, delivers matching maintained Status to new subscribers, removes maintained Status on DEVICE REMOVED and uses property changes to update subscription matching. It is not direct proof of physical health.

Authorization Service can evaluate Registration REQUEST ADD contents; this is separate from Controller-side certificate identity comparison, subsequent ADDED/ERROR registration and physical asset participation.

AZSV-L-0005/0006 return Response SUCCESS for authorized Yes and authorized No. A successful authorization determination is not permission granted, command execution or actual enforced access. L-0007 leaves inability-to-determine policy-dependent.
Authorization granted/denied and the Authorization Service's SUCCESS response are separate from a performing component's command disposition or physical effect.

Authorized valid Discover Request matches maintained Config/Status and reports SUCCESS even with zero matches; inability to perform matching is FAILED. Retrieval of stored Config/Status is distinct from performed sensing and real-time delivery.

Discovery and subscription filtering use source-defined maintained Config/Status and newly received Config/Status/Event/Administrative messages. Property changes may start or stop matching; no universal query syntax or inferred current measurement is added.

Creation includes consumer identity/filter and returns unique subscription ID; creator and consumer may differ. Maintenance while creator registered and cleanup on removed consumer are separately worded; matched messages go to consumer.

New subscriptions receive maintained matching Config and Status as specified by Controller Requirements; earlier DQL initial-cache options remain separately sourced. This is not an Event history cache or proof of universal initial cache behavior.
Maintained Config/Status and newly received Event detector properties affect query/subscription context; detector properties in an Event do not become component Status reports.

Authorization determines permissions; Live Data maintains conditional Config/Status discovery state and routes subscribed messages. Required source service behaviors do not establish their deployed performance or hardware classes.

SUBSCRIPTION ADDED/REMOVED and START/STOP FOLLOWING are Administrative messages to consumers under conditions. LDSV-L-0029 explicitly has contradictory 'Start/now matched' wording with STOP FOLLOWING; retain literal source discrepancy.

registered_blocks.title: Property Mutability
registered_blocks.source_document: ISA Data Model Topics, release 6.0 revision 2, 31 October 2023
registered_blocks.meaning: Parent of §1.1–1.2; explains source mutability as ability to change the property value, not a separate physical device state.
registered_blocks.must_not_imply: No new property kind or deployment state from parent heading.

registered_blocks.title: Mutabilities Overview
registered_blocks.source_document: ISA Data Model Topics, release 6.0 revision 2, 31 October 2023
registered_blocks.meaning: PERMANENT is expected fixed for an operational cycle; READ WRITE value supplied through Set Property; READ ONLY changes through supported dedicated command; WRITE ONLY deprecated for future removal.
registered_blocks.must_not_imply: PERMANENT recommendation to deregister is source 'should', not an ISA universal SHALL; READ WRITE may indirectly trigger physical action without its supplied value changing.

registered_blocks.title: Read Write Versus Read Only
registered_blocks.source_document: ISA Data Model Topics, release 6.0 revision 2, 31 October 2023
registered_blocks.meaning: Table 2 visually checked: only READ WRITE accepts Set Property; only READ ONLY accepts Change/Adjust; PERMANENT accepts neither by those mechanisms. Position then resulting Orientation slew example distinguishes direct assignment from indirect real motion.
registered_blocks.must_not_imply: A Set Property receipt is not proof of requested physical motion; READ ONLY does not imply the supported Change/Adjust command is available for every property.

registered_blocks.title: Event Updates
registered_blocks.source_document: ISA Data Model Topics, release 6.0 revision 2, 31 October 2023
registered_blocks.meaning: Parent contains event update/correlation/recall/resolution rules; source-original Event remains a distributed immutable record.
registered_blocks.must_not_imply: Parent span overlaps children; no double-counted Event definitions or observed instances.

registered_blocks.title: Events Overview
registered_blocks.source_document: ISA Data Model Topics, release 6.0 revision 2, 31 October 2023
registered_blocks.meaning: An Event reports source-observed-world data; a distributed original Event cannot be overwritten across recipients; subsequent Event Update can augment or correct.
registered_blocks.must_not_imply: Source commentary does not establish an immutable database or guaranteed recipient behavior.

registered_blocks.title: Event Update Definition
registered_blocks.source_document: ISA Data Model Topics, release 6.0 revision 2, 31 October 2023
registered_blocks.meaning: Event with optional Event Reference supplied is an Update. Supplied observables take precedence; unmentioned values remain; the original Event time remains the represented observation time while update time dates the update. Multiple updates are ordered by time before application.
registered_blocks.must_not_imply: The simplified ID/Ref table is explanatory; native fingerprint comprises source/time/ID, not a bare identifier or new original observation.

registered_blocks.title: Recalling Events
registered_blocks.source_document: ISA Data Model Topics, release 6.0 revision 2, 31 October 2023
registered_blocks.meaning: Recall is intended for events generated in error or observations not correctable; string reason explains why consumers should disregard referenced Event.
registered_blocks.must_not_imply: A recall notice does not physically erase past messages or prove all consumers complied.

registered_blocks.title: Resolving Events
registered_blocks.source_document: ISA Data Model Topics, release 6.0 revision 2, 31 October 2023
registered_blocks.meaning: Resolve marks a previously accurate Event as no longer requiring attention while using Event Update reference mechanism.
registered_blocks.must_not_imply: Resolved is not recalled/erroneous and not deletion, hardware health, or source-independent event disposition.

registered_blocks.title: Publishing Tracks
registered_blocks.source_document: ISA Data Model Topics, release 6.0 revision 2, 31 October 2023
registered_blocks.meaning: Battle Space Object (BSO) correlates separate Events about the same observed entity, whereas Event Reference corrects a specific Event. Both can occur when correcting/adding BSO of previous Event.
registered_blocks.must_not_imply: BSO is not ISA component UCI, physical asset identity, or an Event correction by itself.

registered_blocks.title: Event Update Examples
registered_blocks.source_document: ISA Data Model Topics, release 6.0 revision 2, 31 October 2023
registered_blocks.meaning: Parent for Figures 2–3, visually inspected on PDF p.14; demonstrates field-level augmenting and recall.
registered_blocks.must_not_imply: Illustrative diagrams are not executed observations or persistence tests.

registered_blocks.title: Augmented State After Applying Event Updates
registered_blocks.source_document: ISA Data Model Topics, release 6.0 revision 2, 31 October 2023
registered_blocks.meaning: Figure 2 retains original event time, combines changed Position, existing Velocity, new Identity and later Media along referenced updates.
registered_blocks.must_not_imply: The resultant augmented state is a consumer interpretation; does not rewrite the published original.

registered_blocks.title: Augmented State After a Recall Event
registered_blocks.source_document: ISA Data Model Topics, release 6.0 revision 2, 31 October 2023
registered_blocks.meaning: Figure 3 displays a Recall indication and carries original time through the augmented event sequence.
registered_blocks.must_not_imply: Diagram does not mandate deletion of all cached or archived original copies.

registered_blocks.title: Resource Descriptors
registered_blocks.source_document: ISA Data Model Topics, release 6.0 revision 2, 31 October 2023
registered_blocks.meaning: Parent describes URL-addressed external material and typed representations, including illustrated media and custom service links.
registered_blocks.must_not_imply: One Resource Descriptor is neither a native CSAPI resource nor proof of current external availability.

registered_blocks.title: Sharing Information on ISA
registered_blocks.source_document: ISA Data Model Topics, release 6.0 revision 2, 31 October 2023
registered_blocks.meaning: Live Data subscription transports native standardized data; non-ISA representations and heavyweight material can be made available on demand through Resource Descriptor.
registered_blocks.must_not_imply: External access URL does not automatically inherit ISA transport, authorization, source authenticity or guaranteed retrieval.

registered_blocks.title: Resource Descriptor Overview and Use Cases
registered_blocks.source_document: ISA Data Model Topics, release 6.0 revision 2, 31 October 2023
registered_blocks.meaning: Resource Descriptor: URL, Resource Type primary/secondary analogous to IANA Media Type, optional title/created/modified/metadata. Example uses image/png; possibilities include native raw data, nonstandard command interface, vCard and KML.
registered_blocks.must_not_imply: Analogy is not a claim that every type is IANA-registered or safe/authorized; custom command interface is not evidence of an executed device command.

registered_blocks.title: Resource Descriptor Usage
registered_blocks.source_document: ISA Data Model Topics, release 6.0 revision 2, 31 October 2023
registered_blocks.meaning: General component resources typically in Status Resources property; observation-related in Event Media observable; may also appear inside custom properties/observables/commands.
registered_blocks.must_not_imply: Status/Media placement is typical not universal; URL/link should not be equated with an original Observation or performed media stream.

registered_blocks.title: Recommended Resource Type Parameters for Video
registered_blocks.source_document: ISA Data Model Topics, release 6.0 revision 2, 31 October 2023
registered_blocks.meaning: Recommended typed NVPs: Bitrate (Mbpsec), Bitrate Control, Codecs (String list), Container, Compression Level, Frame Rate (Hertz), Width/Height (Integer pixels), Scan Type, Audio (Boolean). Compression Level omission/uncompressed caveat is described.
registered_blocks.must_not_imply: These are recommendations, not a guaranteed mandatory video metadata schema, reliable live codec detection, current instrument setting or conversion of other streaming APIs.

registered_blocks.title: Resource Descriptor Examples
registered_blocks.source_document: ISA Data Model Topics, release 6.0 revision 2, 31 October 2023
registered_blocks.meaning: Figures 4–7 and Java API expression are illustrative Resource Descriptor shapes, not verified live endpoints.
registered_blocks.must_not_imply: Do not promote sample localhost data, codec attributes or custom scheme to operational source facts.

registered_blocks.title: Image Download
registered_blocks.source_document: ISA Data Model Topics, release 6.0 revision 2, 31 October 2023
registered_blocks.meaning: Figure 4: localhost image URL, resource type image/png, empty metadata list.
registered_blocks.must_not_imply: Demonstrates a structural example, not a captured image, actual download or authenticated issuer.

registered_blocks.title: Video Stream
registered_blocks.source_document: ISA Data Model Topics, release 6.0 revision 2, 31 October 2023
registered_blocks.meaning: Figure 5 and Java API show a video/mp4 illustrative URL with bitrate 15, frame rate 30, h.264/aac, 1920x1080, PROGRESSIVE and audio=true, plus author metadata.
registered_blocks.must_not_imply: Example values and Java API construction are not an observed stream, implemented transport, runtime verification or installed setting.

registered_blocks.title: Text File with Parameters
registered_blocks.source_document: ISA Data Model Topics, release 6.0 revision 2, 31 October 2023
registered_blocks.meaning: Figure 6: illustrative text/xml URL, charset utf-8 and optional title.
registered_blocks.must_not_imply: A link sample is not proof that the file exists or that the consumer supports its parsing.

registered_blocks.title: Custom Service
registered_blocks.source_document: ISA Data Model Topics, release 6.0 revision 2, 31 October 2023
registered_blocks.meaning: Figure 7: illustrative myprotocol URL and my-service/XYZ resource type with parameter myparam.
registered_blocks.must_not_imply: Does not standardize a transport, security mechanism, controller command or real hardware action.

registered_blocks.title: Further Resources
registered_blocks.source_document: ISA Data Model Topics, release 6.0 revision 2, 31 October 2023
registered_blocks.meaning: ISA Help Desk contact and QR code are source-help context, not data model or normative capabilities.
registered_blocks.must_not_imply: No DIM row or 2023 standard requirement adopted from contact/support information.

source_boundary_notes.finding: PERMANENT change expectation and 'should' deregister versus READ WRITE supplied values and READ ONLY dedicated commands; non-physical Set Property assignment can indirectly trigger physical motion.
source_boundary_notes.handling: Do not make every reported change a physical control action or treat the operational-cycle guidance as a SHALL.

source_boundary_notes.finding: Table3 ID/Ref is an intentionally simplified representation; source specifies normal Event identity as Time/ID/Source.
source_boundary_notes.handling: Do not silently replace original Event Reference with bare Event ID or BSO.

source_boundary_notes.finding: Update time refers to update, while augmented observation keeps original Event time, even with later changed Position.
source_boundary_notes.handling: Never rewrite the original observation time as update time.

source_boundary_notes.finding: Recall signals mistaken report; Resolve signals accurate earlier report no longer requiring attention.
source_boundary_notes.handling: Do not conflate correction, original event retraction, resolution, recipient compliance and physical erasure.

source_boundary_notes.finding: BSO correlates separate Events about an observed entity; Event Reference corrects an Event; rare BSO+Reference used to correct/add BSO.
source_boundary_notes.handling: Not component UCI, track of sensor status or source-verification identity.

source_boundary_notes.finding: Resource Type primary/secondary is analogous to IANA MIME, with custom type/scheme examples.
source_boundary_notes.handling: Do not assert every type is IANA-registered, endpoint reachable or inherently authenticated.

source_boundary_notes.finding: Bitrate/Mbpsec, frame rate/Hertz, Codecs list/String, Audio/Boolean, pixel dimensions and compression-level omission notes are recommended NVP types.
source_boundary_notes.handling: Not mandatory universal codec/stream guarantee or observed running bandwidth.

source_boundary_notes.finding: Figures4–7 use localhost URLs or myprotocol and show structural examples; Figure5/Java example are consistent sample values.
source_boundary_notes.handling: Examples are not real executed media retrievals, commands, ISA certificate policy or CSAPI links.

source_boundary_notes.finding: Revision History Table1 says 6.0r2 updated Resource Descriptor parameter usage and Event Update example.
source_boundary_notes.handling: Do not back-project 6.0r2 examples into older revisions without original evidence.

source_wording_notes.source_literal: What ISA
source_wording_notes.handling: Table2 uses this shortened section3.0 label; the registered/body title remains What ISA Is. Do not create a distinct block.

source_wording_notes.handling: Retain the literal forward-reference wording without inventing missing sections or expanding this delivery. Reviewing the parent own prose does not close its later4.3.7–4.3.16 descendants.

source_wording_notes.finding: The source says Unique Component Identifier rather than ICD/DMS Universal Component Identifier. L0002 says at least one letter; L0006 prohibits consecutive hyphens; plus signs and the supporting-UCI suffix have explicit virtual-component scope.
source_wording_notes.handling: Reuse ISA02-UCI and its completed source credit, preserving source spelling and the exact CMPT rules. No network-only uniqueness, URI, maximum length, ASCII restriction, case folding, physical-device identity or separate virtual-member certificate is inferred.

source_wording_notes.finding: M0003 says a certificate authority approved by ISA; L0010 says an authority acceptable to the organization deploying the component and literally begins The ISA certificate shall use an ISA certificate. CERT3.4 separately assigns deployment certificates to the deploying authority.
source_wording_notes.handling: Keep both levels and the usage-guide context with their own sources. Do not silently replace ISA approval with deployment approval or claim the authorities are identical. Preserve the awkward subject wording without creating a second credential role.

source_wording_notes.finding: M0004 names Elliptical Curve Digital Signature Algorithm (ECDSA), L0011 says ECDSA, while L0013 is titled ECDSA Algorithm but its text says Elliptical Curve Diffie-Hellman (ECDH).
source_wording_notes.handling: Preserve the literal title/text mismatch and source spellings. Do not choose or correct an algorithm, provide an implementation recipe, assert a coherent cryptographic profile, or turn the2023 source into a current recommendation.

source_wording_notes.finding: The title is ECDSA Bit Length, but the specification literally says the ISA certificate shall be at least384 bits long.
source_wording_notes.handling: Retain the subject and bound as written. Do not silently recast this as key size, curve size, signature size, encoded-certificate size, named-curve selection or verified cryptographic strength.

source_wording_notes.finding: The clauses separately address the certificate validity interval and non-revoked state. L0014 says start date prior to the current date; L0015 says end date after it; L0016 glosses currently valid as not revoked.
source_wording_notes.handling: Keep date bounds and revocation distinct. Do not replace prior/after by inclusive comparisons, infer date precision/timezone/skew/revocation-check mechanism, or treat an explanatory revocation gloss as proof that every validity condition is satisfied.

source_wording_notes.finding: Under required-capability parents, Identity and Operating State children say should. Set Observable Reporting says shall if observables are published, and Set Property says shall if settable properties exist. The saved DMS Required bin lists2properties and7commands; its Recommended bin includes Identity,Operating State,Clear Property,Set Property.
source_wording_notes.handling: Preserve each source and its scope instead of rewriting the catalogue membership. Recommended children are not mandatory because of their parent title; conditional Set Property does not become an eighth universal command; the conditional CMPT Set Observable Reporting clause is not silently substituted for the DMS universal wording.

source_wording_notes.finding: The source distinguishes supporting a command from supporting its execution for each applicable declared property. The L0027 explanatory Note associates settable with READ WRITE; L0030 scopes execution to each settable property.
source_wording_notes.handling: Keep declaration/applicability, support, requested execution, authorization and actual effects separate. The READ WRITE Note does not erase the saved PERMANENT/READ ONLY/READ WRITE/WRITE ONLY vocabulary or make every declared property writable.

source_wording: Prior to communicating, the ISA component shall synchronize to a Network Time Protocol (NTP) source.
A Global Positioning System (GPS) may be used in place of an NTP source.
The ISA component should use NTP to synchronize time.
This is not a requirement, but a design goal on the hosting system and network.
source_wording_notes.meaning: Parent shall, GPS substitution and child should/design-goal wording coexist in this edition.
source_wording_notes.interpretation_boundary: Retain all modalities and source scope. Do not make NTP universal, erase pre-communication synchronization, invent a resolution rule between hierarchy levels or supply clock-accuracy numbers.

source_wording: M-0019: within 30 seconds of successfully negotiating an ISA IPL format with the Controller.
L-0055: within 30 seconds of establishing a connection to the Controller.
M-0018 note: An ISA component has reached the connected state upon successfully negotiating an ISA IPL format.
L-0041 initiates Handshake Begin upon establishing a connection.
source_wording_notes.meaning: The two registration deadlines use different printed trigger wording; the connected-state note and earlier handshake trigger provide context without a complete terminology reconciliation.
source_wording_notes.interpretation_boundary: Do not silently choose or equate the anchors. Despite the Completion titles, both timing rules require sending a request rather than successful registration/ADDED within the deadline.

source_wording: M-0010 definition: Synchronize to an NTP source.
L-0031/L-0032 parent reference: Synchronize to an NTP Source
M-0019 definition: Registration Completion Time Constraint
L-0055 parent reference: Registration Completion Time Constrain
source_wording_notes.meaning: Native relationship labels differ in case/punctuation and the final t of Constraint; their referenced IDs still identify the defined requirements.
source_wording_notes.interpretation_boundary: Keep literal titles and reference labels. The valid matching IDs do not become a broken hierarchy or a new requirement.

source_wording: CMPT-L-0048: shall use the smallest Application Data message that can contain the data to be sent.
Saved ICD 4.3.1: message that best fits the application-data size should be used.
source_wording_notes.meaning: The Component Requirements supplies a specific shall framing-size rule alongside the separately preserved ICD should guidance.
source_wording_notes.interpretation_boundary: Attribute each modality to its source; do not rewrite the ICD or convert this to a DMS payload-minimization rule.

source_wording_notes.source_literal: M0026/M0027 call for each ready/reporting state; L0058/L0062 specify all false state values, and L0062 explicitly uses an empty state list to indicate all states of that kind are true.
source_wording_notes.handling: Retain the semantic state obligation and the source-specific false-state snapshot representation. Do not translate this into a universal rule that omitted arbitrary data are true; command states still have only name and ready.

source_wording_notes.source_literal: DMS Config.ccd is structurally optional; CMPT requires CCD in initial Config and the entire CCD on any declaration change. State-change updates carry all false state values.
source_wording_notes.handling: Conditional behavior adds meaning without changing the DMS0–1 field cardinality. Entire CCD means all supported declarations, not all catalogue definitions or a required nonempty category.

source_wording_notes.source_literal: The medium-level update obligations target all connected-to ISA components; L0059 and L0082 name the connected-to ISA Controller.
source_wording_notes.handling: Keep each level’s literal recipient scope. Do not silently replace all components with only Controller or invent direct broadcast/routing behavior.

source_wording_notes.source_literal: Four definitions repeat the Parent Requirements heading; L0063 has no definition in these assigned sections; L0170 is printed after L0082.
source_wording_notes.handling: Preserve all repeated parent groups, source order and native IDs. Do not create a missing numbered requirement or renumber L0170.

source_wording_notes.source_literal: CMPT distinguishes enabled command execution, maintained property value and enabled observable recording. CMPTobservable reporting explicitly names Event; DMS428 reporting description literally says status messages.
source_wording_notes.handling: Carry the established DMS428 wording discrepancy forward with explicit CMPTsupport for Event reporting, without rewriting saved native DMS text. Ready never proves immediate availability, permission, execution or measurement.

source_wording_notes.source_literal: L0082 following CCD-bearing update says every declared reporting-true property, while initial/periodic rules require ready=true and reporting=true, and ICD7.3 says NotReady properties must be NotReporting and absent fromStatus.
source_wording_notes.handling: Preserve the exact predicates and separate full post-update Status from periodic change-only Status. Reuse ICDqualification without silently inserting ready into L0082 or applying change-only selection to full reports.

source_wording_notes.source_literal: CMPT M0032 associates operational state and permitted traffic with receipt of initial Status; SDD6.3.2 Table5 and Figure5 enter Operational upon receiving initial Config, while SDD Figure16 reaches its Operational endpoint after initial Status.
source_wording_notes.handling: Retain the already recorded SDD internal difference and the explicit CMPT message gate/discard requirements. Do not silently harmonize phases or claim a secure connection or received Config alone lifts the CMPT gate.

source_wording_notes.source_literal: Initial Status is triggered/timed by sending initial configuration; M0033 note separately says configured state follows receiving the Controller initial configuration.
source_wording_notes.handling: Keep sending and receiving triggers distinct; do not replace the 30-second trigger with receipt of ControllerConfig or infer an additional wait.

source_wording_notes.source_literal: CMPT uses 30 seconds after sending Config for initial/full-update Status and a conditional 500ms bound after eligible property change. SDD6.3.3.4.2 initial Status receipt-time prose says since registered, while Figure11 timer annotation says after receiving registrant Config and Figure17 names Initial Status Receipt Timer.
source_wording_notes.handling: Attribute component send obligations and Controller receipt timers independently, preserving the saved SDD-FLOW-N02 trigger difference. Do not merge source timers, invent values or treat 500ms as a universal periodic interval or network-delivery guarantee.

source_wording_notes.source_literal: Initial Status carries every ready/reporting property; periodic Status carries all and only changed ready/reporting properties; never-reported values count as changed. ICD6.5 broadly says current values must always be provided.
source_wording_notes.handling: Qualify the broad overview with these explicit selection rules. The periodic heartbeat obligation does not vanish when no properties changed; the saved DMS0+ collection and SDD no-change flow permit an empty periodic property report. DMS215 Get Status separately returns declared ready properties even when reporting is disabled; do not apply publication selection to that command result.

source_wording_notes.source_literal: CMPTgives periodic minimum/maximum bounds and a conditional change trigger; DMS329/334 threshold definitions say Status publication regardless of status interval.
source_wording_notes.handling: Retain threshold exception wording beside general periodic rules without inventing precedence, Boolean threshold combinations, interval clamps, jitter allowance or a single reconciled implementation algorithm.

source_wording_notes.source_literal: The M0036 note says a property-appropriate change delta needs to be established and the implementer should consider consumer-interesting changes; it supplies no numeric tolerance or unit.
source_wording_notes.handling: Retain SHOULD in the note separately from SHALL in the requirement. Do not manufacture a universal threshold, sampling frequency or assurance of a complete intervening-value history.

source_wording_notes.source_literal: CMPT M0038/M0039 say full status after non-responsiveness, while L0100 selects every declared property whose ready and reporting states are true.
source_wording_notes.handling: Preserve both source levels. Treat the low-level selection as the explicit message-content rule without rewriting the higher-level phrase into every declared property.

source_wording_notes.source_literal: REVIVED handling requires a complete configuration set and a 30-second send limit from the REVIVED Registration notification.
source_wording_notes.handling: Record recovery Config as a source send obligation, not proof of network receipt, acceptance, implementation health or a new persistent configuration object.

source_wording_notes.source_literal: Service-recommendation support is conditional on requiring an ISA service; Set Live Data Service and Set Authorization Service have their own stated conditions.
source_wording_notes.handling: Do not convert optional/conditional service use into mandatory activation or a permanent service dependency for every component.

source_wording_notes.source_literal: Discovery and subscription requirements use should for a previously recommended Live Data Service instance.
source_wording_notes.handling: Retain should rather than strengthening it to shall. A recommendation is routing guidance, not proof that discovery/subscription succeeded or that a provider is permanently bound.

source_wording_notes.source_literal: Subscription creation carries desired filters and a locally unique name; cancellation cites the subscription ID and the Live Data Service instance where it was created.
source_wording_notes.handling: Keep subscription definition/identity, creation/removal requests and actual delivered data separate.

source_wording_notes.source_literal: Event detector-property context may include relevant property values changed since last Status; the Note explicitly says including them in Event does not count as a Status update.
source_wording_notes.handling: Keep Event context and Status reporting separate; do not treat contextual property values as a replacement heartbeat or persistent state update.

source_wording_notes.source_literal: Event publication has a 500ms send bound after making the observation.
source_wording_notes.handling: Record this as a publication-latency obligation. It does not alter Event.time occurrence semantics or prove receipt/processing within 500ms.

source_wording_notes.source_literal: Observation update and recall use Event Reference; updates may include relevant observables not present in the previous Event, while recalls include Recall.
source_wording_notes.handling: Preserve lineage to the cited Event. Do not model update as a new unrelated event or recall as deletion of source history.

source_wording_notes.source_literal: On consuming an update, in-use observables from the cited Event are replaced as appropriate; on recall, use of the cited contents ceases. Notes say the treatment is usage/system specific.
source_wording_notes.handling: Do not invent universal database deletion, archival removal or immutable replacement behavior beyond the source's use semantics.

source_wording_notes.source_literal: A declared ready command is supported, but a valid request may still encounter temporary unavailability, queueing, BUSY, QUEUED or IN PROGRESS before final SUCCESS/FAILED.
source_wording_notes.handling: Keep readiness, immediate availability, queueing, response state, execution and achieved physical effect separate.

source_wording_notes.source_literal: Initial near-real-time command Response is due within 200ms; non-real-time initial Response is due within the performing component's Minimum Status Interval. Queued and long-running updates use the Minimum/Maximum Status Interval bounds.
source_wording_notes.handling: Retain the source-specific response timing and command classes; do not reinterpret the status-interval properties as only Status-message cadence or as execution completion deadlines.

source_wording_notes.source_literal: Commanding limits Requests to commands declared in the target CCD with ready state true and requires all needed input arguments.
source_wording_notes.handling: Treat declaration/readiness as request eligibility, not authorization, execution, success or physical-effect evidence.

source_wording_notes.source_literal: A virtual ISA component is an entity represented on the ISA network by another ISA component; DEVICE ADDED/REMOVED, Config, Status, Event and command behavior can all be emitted on its behalf.
source_wording_notes.handling: Model this as network representation/source attribution, not proof of physical containment, independent hardware identity, separate certificate or direct ISA interface.

source_wording_notes.source_literal: Virtual-command enablement may be implemented by execution on behalf of the virtual component, translation to a non-ISA message, or forwarding an ISA Request; these are examples in a Note.
source_wording_notes.handling: Keep mediation method separate from command semantics and do not infer a required transport or a permanent physical architecture from the examples.

source_wording_notes.source_literal: Disconnecting requires active subscriptions removed and deregistration requested; control-lock release is should. M0073 says should terminate the connection after Registration Removed, while L0168 says the component may close and notes the socket may remain open.
source_wording_notes.handling: Preserve deregistration and connection closure as separate steps and retain should/may wording rather than forcing a mandatory socket close.

source_wording_notes.source_literal: Appendix A defines Analysis, Demonstration, Inspection and Test, but its low-level requirement table contains165 mappings:145 Test and20 Inspection. CMPT-L-0164 is defined in §4.3.15 but absent from the table.
source_wording_notes.handling: Retain the Appendix as source conformance guidance and record the L0164 omission as a local source discrepancy. Do not assign an inferred verification method or turn verification method into runtime system data.

Authorization failure/unavailability uses effective policy; source example may authorize none or all, no universal default.
Maintain Config/Status only if sufficient computing resources; do not assert unlimited cache.
DEVICE REMOVED clears maintained Config/Status, not original historical observation records.

PERMANENT change expectation and 'should' deregister versus READ WRITE supplied values and READ ONLY dedicated commands; non-physical Set Property assignment can indirectly trigger physical motion. Do not make every reported change a physical control action or treat the operational-cycle guidance as a SHALL.
Table3 ID/Ref is an intentionally simplified representation; source specifies normal Event identity as Time/ID/Source. Do not silently replace original Event Reference with bare Event ID or BSO.
Update time refers to update, while augmented observation keeps original Event time, even with later changed Position. Never rewrite the original observation time as update time.

Recall signals mistaken report; Resolve signals accurate earlier report no longer requiring attention. Do not conflate correction, original event retraction, resolution, recipient compliance and physical erasure.

BSO correlates separate Events about an observed entity; Event Reference corrects an Event; rare BSO+Reference used to correct/add BSO. Not component UCI, track of sensor status or source-verification identity.
Resource Type primary/secondary is analogous to IANA MIME, with custom type/scheme examples. Do not assert every type is IANA-registered, endpoint reachable or inherently authenticated.

Bitrate/Mbpsec, frame rate/Hertz, Codecs list/String, Audio/Boolean, pixel dimensions and compression-level omission notes are recommended NVP types. Not mandatory universal codec/stream guarantee or observed running bandwidth.

Figures4–7 use localhost URLs or myprotocol and show structural examples; Figure5/Java example are consistent sample values. Examples are not real executed media retrievals, commands, ISA certificate policy or CSAPI links.
