display: ISA component: virtual node; Client / Controller roles; Controller software responsibilities
before.definition: A network participant has client or Controller responsibilities, separately from the generic identity of the participant and any physical equipment it represents.
before.boundary: A Controller is software; a component may be a sensor, adapter, base station or command-and-control system. A virtual node is not necessarily one physical device. The original network-participant mapping receives supporting evidence but retains its broader architecture reconciliation assignment.

display: All ISA components support the client-side connection role; Controllers also support the server-side role
after.definition: Client-side and server-side identify roles in a connection. Every ISA component, including a Controller, supports initiating connections to a Controller; Controllers also accept connections.
after.boundary: The initiator is the client and the non-initiator is the server for that connection. Controller is a service responsibility and software role; it also has client-side responsibilities. These are not disjoint equipment classes, physical device counts or process counts. A visible network participant need not equal one physical device.

master_revisions.reason: Detailed SDD roles refine the introductory Client/Controller shorthand without changing source meaning or making a case implementation claim.

before.definition: A participant belongs to a virtual network instance and communicates through the described connections; instances may interconnect across locations.

after.definition: A local ISA instance and the broader network describe virtual participation and connections; local Controller/client instances may interconnect across locations.
after.boundary: The Introductory Guide local instance has one Controller and clients. SDD describes a broader network of interconnected components and Controllers over existing physical networks, with one or many Controllers in a deployment. Do not make a local instance a global one-Controller limit or infer physical containment, an actual deployment inventory, tested topology or mandatory full-mesh connectivity.

master_revisions.source_qualification: AZSV-L-0005/0006 return Response SUCCESS for authorized Yes and authorized No. A successful authorization determination is not permission granted, command execution or actual enforced access. L-0007 leaves inability-to-determine policy-dependent.
Authorization granted/denied and the Authorization Service's SUCCESS response are separate from a performing component's command disposition or physical effect.

Authorization Service can evaluate Registration REQUEST ADD contents; this is separate from Controller-side certificate identity comparison, subsequent ADDED/ERROR registration and physical asset participation.

Authorization determines permissions; Live Data maintains conditional Config/Status discovery state and routes subscribed messages. Required source service behaviors do not establish their deployed performance or hardware classes.

Live Data caches new Config information only if sufficient computing resources exist, transmits maintained matching Config on subscription creation and removes maintained Config on DEVICE REMOVED. This is not original source-history erasure.

Live Data maintains new Status information only if resources permit, delivers matching maintained Status to new subscribers, removes maintained Status on DEVICE REMOVED and uses property changes to update subscription matching. It is not direct proof of physical health.

Authorized valid Discover Request matches maintained Config/Status and reports SUCCESS even with zero matches; inability to perform matching is FAILED. Retrieval of stored Config/Status is distinct from performed sensing and real-time delivery.

Discovery and subscription filtering use source-defined maintained Config/Status and newly received Config/Status/Event/Administrative messages. Property changes may start or stop matching; no universal query syntax or inferred current measurement is added.

Creation includes consumer identity/filter and returns unique subscription ID; creator and consumer may differ. Maintenance while creator registered and cleanup on removed consumer are separately worded; matched messages go to consumer.

New subscriptions receive maintained matching Config and Status as specified by Controller Requirements; earlier DQL initial-cache options remain separately sourced. This is not an Event history cache or proof of universal initial cache behavior.
Maintained Config/Status and newly received Event detector properties affect query/subscription context; detector properties in an Event do not become component Status reports.

An Event's detector-property values can cause a subscription to start or stop matching without themselves constituting a Status update, actual physical part change or original observation-result provenance.

SUBSCRIPTION ADDED/REMOVED and START/STOP FOLLOWING are Administrative messages to consumers under conditions. LDSV-L-0029 explicitly has contradictory 'Start/now matched' wording with STOP FOLLOWING; retain literal source discrepancy.

DEVICE REMOVED causes Live Data maintained Config/Status cleanup and subscription consumer cleanup; network/cache lifecycle is distinct from physical hardware removal or historical observation deletion.

DEVICE REMOVED leads Live Data to discard retained Config/Status information for the cited participant; that is a service-visible state change, not proof of physical composition change or equipment destruction.

Authorization granted/denied and the Authorization Service's SUCCESS response are separate from a performing component's command disposition or physical effect.

Authorization Service can evaluate Registration REQUEST ADD contents; this is separate from Controller-side certificate identity comparison, subsequent ADDED/ERROR registration and physical asset participation.

Authorization determines permissions; Live Data maintains conditional Config/Status discovery state and routes subscribed messages. Required source service behaviors do not establish their deployed performance or hardware classes.

Live Data caches new Config information only if sufficient computing resources exist, transmits maintained matching Config on subscription creation and removes maintained Config on DEVICE REMOVED. This is not original source-history erasure.

Live Data maintains new Status information only if resources permit, delivers matching maintained Status to new subscribers, removes maintained Status on DEVICE REMOVED and uses property changes to update subscription matching. It is not direct proof of physical health.

Authorized valid Discover Request matches maintained Config/Status and reports SUCCESS even with zero matches; inability to perform matching is FAILED. Retrieval of stored Config/Status is distinct from performed sensing and real-time delivery.

Discovery and subscription filtering use source-defined maintained Config/Status and newly received Config/Status/Event/Administrative messages. Property changes may start or stop matching; no universal query syntax or inferred current measurement is added.

Creation includes consumer identity/filter and returns unique subscription ID; creator and consumer may differ. Maintenance while creator registered and cleanup on removed consumer are separately worded; matched messages go to consumer.

New subscriptions receive maintained matching Config and Status as specified by Controller Requirements; earlier DQL initial-cache options remain separately sourced. This is not an Event history cache or proof of universal initial cache behavior.
Maintained Config/Status and newly received Event detector properties affect query/subscription context; detector properties in an Event do not become component Status reports.

An Event's detector-property values can cause a subscription to start or stop matching without themselves constituting a Status update, actual physical part change or original observation-result provenance.

SUBSCRIPTION ADDED/REMOVED and START/STOP FOLLOWING are Administrative messages to consumers under conditions. LDSV-L-0029 explicitly has contradictory 'Start/now matched' wording with STOP FOLLOWING; retain literal source discrepancy.

DEVICE REMOVED causes Live Data maintained Config/Status cleanup and subscription consumer cleanup; network/cache lifecycle is distinct from physical hardware removal or historical observation deletion.

DEVICE REMOVED leads Live Data to discard retained Config/Status information for the cited participant; that is a service-visible state change, not proof of physical composition change or equipment destruction.

master_revisions.source_qualification: PERMANENT operational-cycle expectation and recommended deregistration differ from READ WRITE supplied knowledge through Set Property and READ ONLY values altered via a separately supported Change/Adjust command. Supplying Position may indirectly cause Orientation motion while Position remains READ WRITE.
Mutability labels describe how a reported property value can be changed, not the physical nature of a component, a guarantee of a supported actuation command or a universal authorization outcome.

Set Property supplies a READ WRITE property value as information about a component; the example distinguishes that assignment from later indirect physical slewing. It does not itself prove actuator effect.

Event Reference targets the original Event fingerprint (normally Time, ID, Source), whereas BSO correlates multiple Events about an observed entity. An illustrative simplified ID column is not an exhaustive native identity schema.

An updated/augmented Event retains its original observation time; update's own time dates that update. Multiple updates to the same source event are ordered by time before combining, not converted into new original observation times.
Recall reason pertains to a mistaken original Event; it asks recipients to disregard the Event, without establishing erasure, universal recipient compliance or the same meaning as Resolve.
Resolve indicates a formerly accurate Event no longer requires attention; it is distinct from Recall for erroneous Events, physical equipment cessation and archive deletion.

BSO correlates successive Events about the same observed entity (track); Event Reference addresses a prior Event for correction. Co-occurrence is allowed when correcting/adding BSO. BSO does not identify an ISA component.

Event Media typically holds Resource Descriptors to related external media. A URL/Resource Type/metadata description is not a performed Observation, provenance authentication or guaranteed media delivery.

Status Resources typically supplies Resource Descriptors to component-provided material; a descriptor has URL, primary/secondary Resource Type and optional metadata. Current reachability and original issuer authenticity are not established.
Observed-entity track correlation should use BSO, not Event Reference for updates to the same Event; a video track identifier cannot be equated without native scope evidence.
Event Update observables update the augmented event view selectively; unmentioned values persist in the combined interpretation, but Event detector-property context does not become a Status record.

Original Event reference and BSO observed-entity correlation have different targets and reuse rules. Neither proves cryptographic source authenticity or makes four digital copies four original Events.
Event observables are observation-associated content; update-reference semantics and partial replacement differ from Config declarations and property Status values.

The guide describes general Resource Descriptors typically published as Status Resources; descriptive location/typed link is not evidence of a current reachable URL or actual component physical state.
